title.zh: 卷19 列傳第11 達奚武 子震 侯莫陳順 豆盧寧 宇文貴 楊忠 王雄
title.en: Volume 19 Biographies 11: Da Xiwu; Zi Zhen; Houmo Chenshun; Dou Luning; Yu Wengui; Yang Zhong; Wang Xiong
title.raw: 卷19 列傳第11 達奚武 子震 侯莫陳順 豆盧寧 宇文貴 楊忠 王雄 Volume 19 Biographies 11: Da Xiwu; Zi Zhen; Houmo Chenshun; Dou Luning; Yu Wengui; Yang Zhong; Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 達奚武 子震 侯莫陳順 豆盧寧 宇文貴 楊忠 王雄

translations.literal: Da Xiwu; Zi Zhen; Houmo Chen Shun; Dou Luning; Yuwen Gui; Yang Zhong; Wang Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu — Zi Zhen — Houmo Chen Shun — Dou Luning — Yuwen Gui — Yang Zhong — Wang Xiong

sentences.zh: 達奚武字成興，代人也。

translations.literal: Da Xiwu, styled Chenxing, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu, styled Chenxing, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖眷，魏懷荒鎮將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Juan was garrison commander of Huaihuang under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Juan had been garrison commander of Huaihuang under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父長，汧城鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Chang was garrison commander of Qiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang served as garrison commander of Qiancheng.

sentences.zh: 武少倜儻，好馳射，為賀拔岳所知。

translations.literal: Wu in youth was unconventional and free-spirited, fond of riding and archery, and was recognized by He Ba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Da Xiwu was bold and independent, loved horsemanship and archery, and caught the attention of He Ba Yue.

sentences.zh: 岳征關右，引為別將，武遂委心事之。

translations.literal: When Yue campaigned in Guan-you, he brought Wu in as a separate commander; Wu then devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ba Yue marched into Guan-you he made Da Xiwu a separate commander, and Da Xiwu gave himself entirely to his service.

sentences.zh: 以戰功拜羽林監、子都督。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed overseer of the Feathered Forest guard and cadet commander.
translations.idiomatic: For battlefield achievements he received the posts of overseer of the Feathered Forest guard and cadet commander.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，武與趙貴收岳屍歸平涼，同翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmo Chen Yue, Wu together with Zhao Gui recovered Yue's corpse and returned to Pingliang, jointly supporting and raising up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmo Chen Yue murdered He Ba Yue, Da Xiwu and Zhao Gui recovered the body and returned to Pingliang, where they helped install Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 從平悅，除中散大夫、都督，封須昌縣伯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Yue, he was appointed palace attendant for loose conduct and commander, enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was put down, Da Xiwu was made palace attendant for loose conduct and commander, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武入關，授直寢，轉大丞相府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered Guan, he was granted direct-pavilion duty and transferred to military affairs staff officer in the grand chancellor's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west into Guan, Da Xiwu was given direct-pavilion duty and made a military staff officer in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's chancellery.

sentences.zh: 大統初，出為東秦州刺史，加散騎常侍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he was sent out as governor of East Qinzhou, given additional rank as attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry, and his nobility was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he became governor of East Qinzhou, was given the additional title attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry, and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 齊神武與竇泰、高敖曹三道來侵，太祖欲幷兵擊竇泰，諸將多異議，唯武及蘇綽與太祖意同，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan together with Dou Tai and Gao Aocao came invading on three routes; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to combine forces and strike Dou Tai; the generals mostly had differing opinions—only Wu and Su Chuo agreed with the Grand Progenitor's intent, and they thereupon captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan invaded on three fronts with Dou Tai and Gao Aocao, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wanted to concentrate and destroy Dou Tai. Most of his generals disagreed, but Da Xiwu and Su Chuo sided with him, and Dou Tai was taken.

sentences.zh: 齊神武乃退。

translations.literal: Gao Huan thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then retreated.

sentences.zh: 太祖進圖弘農，遣武從兩騎覘候動靜，武與其候騎遇，卽便交戰，斬六級，獲三人而反。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai advanced to target Hongnong and sent Wu with two horsemen to scout movements; Wu encountered their scout cavalry and immediately joined battle, beheading six, capturing three men, and returning.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pressed toward Hongnong he sent Da Xiwu with two riders to reconnoiter. Da Xiwu ran into enemy scouts, fought at once, took six heads and three prisoners, and returned.

sentences.zh: 齊神武趣沙苑，太祖復遣武覘之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan hastened toward Shayuan; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again sent Wu to scout him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan pushed toward Shayuan, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Da Xiwu out to scout once more.

sentences.zh: 武從三騎，皆衣敵人衣服。

translations.literal: Wu took three horsemen, all wearing enemy clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu took three men, all dressed in enemy uniforms.

sentences.zh: 至日暮，去營百步，下馬潛聽，得其軍號。

translations.literal: Reaching dusk, one hundred paces from the camp, he dismounted and listened secretly, obtaining their camp passwords.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, a hundred paces from the camp, he dismounted and eavesdropped until he learned their night watchwords.

sentences.zh: 因上馬歷營，若警夜者，有不如法者，往往撻之。

translations.literal: He then mounted and rode through the camps as if a night-watch officer; those who did not conform to regulations he often whipped.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rode through the camps posing as a night patrol. Anyone out of order he flogged on the spot.

sentences.zh: 具知敵之情狀，以告太祖。

translations.literal: He fully learned the enemy's situation and reported it to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Having mapped the enemy's disposition in full, he reported back to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖深嘉焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor deeply praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 遂從破之。

translations.literal: He then followed and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu then joined the battle and helped rout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 除大都督，進爵高陽郡公，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand commander, his nobility advanced to Duke of Gaoyang commandery, and given the ranks of grand general of chariots and cavalry and feoffal peer with ceremonial parity of three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander, promoted to Duke of Gaoyang, and given the titles of grand general of chariots and cavalry and feoffal peer with ceremonial parity of three offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，太祖援洛陽，武率騎一千為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai came to the relief of Luoyang; Wu led one thousand horsemen as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 4, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to relieve Luoyang, and Da Xiwu led a thousand horsemen as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至穀城，與李弼破莫多婁貸文。

translations.literal: Reaching Gucheng, together with Li Bi he defeated Modu Lou Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: At Gucheng he and Li Bi broke the force of Modu Lou Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 進至河橋，武又力戰，斬其司徒高敖曹。

translations.literal: Advancing to Heqiao, Wu again fought fiercely and beheaded their minister of education Gao Aocao.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing on to Heqiao, Da Xiwu fought hard again and killed Gao Aocao, Gao Huan's minister of education.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, and opening-the-feudatory with ceremonial parity of three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, and opening-the-feudatory with ceremonial parity of three offices.

sentences.zh: 出為北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as governor of North Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned governor of North Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 復戰邙山，時大軍不利，齊神武乘勝進至陝。

translations.literal: He fought again at Mount Mang; at that time the main army fared poorly; Gao Huan seized victory and advanced as far as Shan.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang the main army faltered again. Gao Huan pressed the advantage and pushed to Shan.

sentences.zh: 武率兵禦之，乃退。

translations.literal: Wu led troops to resist him, and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu led troops to block him, and Gao Huan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time, his rank was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔武率兵三萬，經略漢川。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict ordered Wu to lead thirty thousand troops to secure the Han River basin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 an edict sent Da Xiwu with thirty thousand men to subdue the Han River region.

sentences.zh: 梁將楊賢以武興降，梁深以白馬降，武分兵守其城。

translations.literal: Liang general Yang Xian surrendered Wuxing; Liang Shen surrendered Baima; Wu divided troops to garrison those cities.
translations.idiomatic: Liang generals Yang Xian and Liang Shen surrendered Wuxing and Baima. Da Xiwu left detachments to hold both towns.

sentences.zh: 梁梁州刺史、宜豐侯蕭循固守南鄭，武圍之數旬，循乃請服，武為解圍。

translations.literal: Liang Governor of Liang Province and Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun firmly held Nanzheng; Wu besieged it for several tens of days; Xun then requested submission, and Wu lifted the siege for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xun, Liang governor of Liang Province and Marquis of Yifeng, held Nanzheng stubbornly. Da Xiwu besieged the city for weeks until Xiao Xun offered to submit, and Da Xiwu lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 會梁武陵王蕭紀遣其將楊乾運等將兵萬餘人救循，循於是更據城不出。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji sent his general Yang Qianyun and others with more than ten thousand troops to rescue Xun; Xun thereupon again held the city and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liang Prince Xiao Ji of Wuling sent Yang Qianyun with more than ten thousand men to relieve Xiao Xun, and Xiao Xun shut the gates again.

sentences.zh: 恐援軍之至，表裏受敵，乃簡精騎三千，逆擊乾運于白馬，大破之。

translations.literal: Fearing the arrival of relief troops and being attacked from without and within, he selected three thousand elite horsemen and met Qianyun at Baima in a counterstrike, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing encirclement when the relief force arrived, Da Xiwu picked three thousand crack horsemen and intercepted Yang Qianyun at Baima, routing him completely.

sentences.zh: 乾運退走。

translations.literal: Qianyun withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianyun fled.

sentences.zh: 武乃陳蜀軍俘級於城下。

translations.literal: Wu then displayed Shu-army captives and heads before the city.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu then paraded Liang prisoners and severed heads beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 循知援軍被破，乃降，率所部男女三萬口入朝，自剱以北悉平。

translations.literal: Xun learning the relief army had been defeated, then submitted; he led his followers, men and women numbering thirty thousand mouths, to enter court audience; from Zijian northward all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xun learned the relief army was broken, he surrendered and led thirty thousand people into court submission. Everything north of Zijian was now pacified.

sentences.zh: 明年，武振旅還京師。

translations.literal: The next year, Wu returned the army in triumph to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Da Xiwu brought his army home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 朝議初欲以武為柱國，武謂人曰：「我作柱國，不應在元子孝前。

translations.literal: At court it was first proposed to make Wu a pillar of state; Wu said to people: "If I become a pillar of state, I should not rank before Yuan Zixiao.
translations.idiomatic: The court first planned to make Da Xiwu a pillar of state. He said: "As a pillar of state I should not rank above Yuan Zixiao.

sentences.zh: 」固辭不受。

translations.literal: "He firmly declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: "He stood firm and refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍出鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: As grand general he was sent out to garrison Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: He left office as grand general to garrison Yubi.

sentences.zh: 武乃量地形勝，立樂昌、胡營、新城三防。

translations.literal: Wu then measured the terrain's advantages and established three fortifications: Lechang, Huying, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu studied the ground and built three defensive posts at Lechang, Huying, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 齊將高苟子以千騎攻新城，武邀擊之，悉虜其衆。

translations.literal: Qi general Gao Gouzi with one thousand horsemen attacked Xincheng; Wu intercepted and struck him, capturing his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi general Gao Gouzi attacked Xincheng with a thousand horsemen, Da Xiwu ambushed him and took every man.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜柱國、大司寇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Wu was appointed pillar of state and grand minister of crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Da Xiwu was made pillar of state and grand minister of crime.

sentences.zh: 齊北豫州刺史司馬消難舉州來附，詔武與楊忠迎消難以歸。

translations.literal: Qi Governor of North Yuzhou Sima Xiaonan raised the province to come over in allegiance; an edict ordered Wu together with Yang Zhong to welcome Xiaonan back.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi governor Sima Xiaonan of North Yuzhou defected with his province, an edict sent Da Xiwu and Yang Zhong to escort him in.

sentences.zh: 武成初，轉大宗伯，進封鄭國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, and his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Zheng with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wucheng era he became grand master of ceremonies and was advanced to Duke of Zheng with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 齊將斛律敦侵汾、絳，武以萬騎禦之，敦退。

translations.literal: Qi general Hulu Dun invaded Fen and Jiang; Wu with ten thousand horsemen resisted him, and Dun withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi general Hulu Dun raided Fen and Jiang, Da Xiwu met him with ten thousand cavalry and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 武築栢壁城，留開府權嚴、薛羽生守之。

translations.literal: Wu built Baibi city and left opening-the-feudatory Quan Yan and Xue Yusheng to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu built Baibi fortress and left Quan Yan and Xue Yusheng, both with opening-the-feudatory rank, to hold it.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，遷太保。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was transferred to grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3 he was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍東伐。

translations.literal: That year, the main army campaigned east.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the court launched an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 隨公楊忠引突厥自北道，武以三萬騎自東道，期會晉陽。

translations.literal: Duke of Sui Yang Zhong led the Turks by the northern route; Wu with thirty thousand horsemen by the eastern route, with a rendezvous fixed at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yang Zhong of Sui brought the Turks down the northern route while Da Xiwu led thirty thousand horsemen eastward, planning to meet at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 武至平陽，後期不進，而忠已還，武尚未知。

translations.literal: Wu reached Pingyang but, past the deadline, did not advance; meanwhile Zhong had already returned, and Wu did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu reached Pingyang but failed to push forward after the rendezvous date. Yang Zhong had already withdrawn, and Da Xiwu did not yet know it.

sentences.zh: 齊將斛律明月遺武書曰：「鴻鶴已翔於寥廓，羅者猶視於沮澤也。

translations.literal: Qi general Hulu Mingyue sent Wu a letter saying: "The swan and crane have already soared into the vast sky; the fowler still gazes at the marsh."
translations.idiomatic: Qi general Hulu Mingyue wrote Da Xiwu: "The swan has already risen into the open sky, yet the fowler still stares at the bog."

sentences.zh: 」武覽書，乃班師。

translations.literal: Wu reading the letter, thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the letter, Da Xiwu turned his army around and marched home.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，從晉公護東伐。

translations.literal: The next year, he followed Duke of Jin Hu on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Duke Hu of Jin on the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 時尉遲迥圍洛陽，為敵所敗。

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Jiong besieged Luoyang and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong was then besieging Luoyang when the enemy broke him.

sentences.zh: 武與齊王憲於邙山禦之。

translations.literal: Wu together with Prince of Qi Xian resisted them at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu and Prince Yuwen Xian of Qi blocked the pursuit at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 至夜，收軍。

translations.literal: At nightfall, they gathered the army.
translations.idiomatic: At night they pulled the troops in.

sentences.zh: 憲欲待明更戰，武欲還，固爭未決。

translations.literal: Xian wished to wait for dawn and fight again; Wu wished to return; they argued stubbornly and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian wanted to wait for daylight and fight again. Da Xiwu wanted to withdraw. They argued fiercely without reaching a decision.

sentences.zh: 武曰：「洛陽軍散，人情駭動。

translations.literal: Wu said: "At Luoyang the army is scattered; morale is shaken and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu said: "The army at Luoyang is broken and the men are terrified.

sentences.zh: 若不因夜速還，明日欲歸不得。

translations.literal: If we do not use the night to return quickly, tomorrow we will wish to go home and will not be able.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not march tonight, by tomorrow we will not get home at all.

sentences.zh: 武在軍旅久矣，備見形勢。

translations.literal: Wu has long been in the army and has fully seen how situations unfold.
translations.idiomatic: I have soldiered for years and seen how these situations turn.

sentences.zh: 大王少年未經事，豈可將數營士衆，一旦棄之乎。

translations.literal: Your Highness is young and has not yet experienced affairs—how can one take several camps of officers and soldiers and in one stroke abandon them?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is young and untested. How can you abandon several camps of men in a single moment?"

sentences.zh: 」憲從之，遂全軍而返。

translations.literal: Xian followed him, and they then returned with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian yielded, and the entire force got back safely.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，轉太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was transferred to grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 3 Da Xiwu became grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 武賤時，奢侈好華飾。

translations.literal: When Wu was lowly in station, he was extravagant and fond of fine adornment.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Da Xiwu had been fond of luxury and show.

sentences.zh: 及居重位，不持威儀，行常單馬，左右止一兩人而已。

translations.literal: When he reached high position, he did not maintain imposing ceremonial; when traveling he usually rode alone, with only one or two attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rose to high office he dropped all ceremonial display. He usually rode alone with only one or two men at his side.

sentences.zh: 外門不施戟，恆晝掩一扉。

translations.literal: At the outer gate he did not set halberds; by day he always kept only one leaf of the gate closed.
translations.idiomatic: He posted no halberds at his gate and always left only one door panel shut even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 或謂武曰：「公位冠群後，功名蓋世，出入儀衛，須稱具瞻，何輕率若是？

translations.literal: Someone said to Wu: "Your Lordship's rank crowns the court nobles; your merit and fame surpass the age; going out and entering, guards and escort ought to match what all look to—why so careless and light as this?
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Da Xiwu: "Your rank leads the nobles and your fame fills the age. A man in your position should look the part when he goes abroad. Why carry yourself so casually?

sentences.zh: 」武曰：「子之言，非吾心也。

translations.literal: Wu said: "Your words do not accord with my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu answered: "That is not how I see it.

sentences.zh: 吾在布衣，豈望富貴，不可頓忘疇昔。

translations.literal: When I was in plain cloth, how could I have looked for wealth and honor—I cannot suddenly forget former days.
translations.idiomatic: When I wore plain cloth I never dreamed of wealth. I cannot forget that overnight.

sentences.zh: 且天下未平，國恩未報，安可過事威容乎。

translations.literal: Moreover the realm is not yet pacified; the state's grace is not yet repaid—how can one overindulge in imposing display?"
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled and I have not yet repaid the state's kindness. How can I fuss over pomp and ceremony?"

sentences.zh: 」言者慙而退。

translations.literal: The speaker ashamed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The man withdrew in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 武之在同州也，時屬天旱，高祖勑武祀華岳，岳廟舊在山下，常所禱祈。

translations.literal: When Wu was at Tongzhou, there was drought at the time; Emperor Gaozu ordered Wu to sacrifice to Mount Hua; the mountain's temple was formerly at the foot, the usual place for prayer.
translations.idiomatic: While Da Xiwu governed Tong Province a drought struck. Emperor Yuwen Yong ordered him to pray at Mount Hua, whose shrine stood at the foot of the peak—the usual place for such rites.

sentences.zh: 武謂僚屬曰：「吾備位三公，不能燮理陰陽，遂使盛農之月，久絕甘雨，天子勞心，百姓惶懼。

translations.literal: Wu told his staff: "I occupy a place among the three dukes yet cannot harmonize yin and yang, so that in the height of farming months long there has been no sweet rain; the Son of Heaven is troubled at heart and the common people are fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu told his staff: "I hold one of the three highest offices yet have failed to set heaven and earth in order, so that in the heart of the farming season the rains have stopped, the emperor is anxious, and the people are terrified.

sentences.zh: 忝寄旣重，憂責實深。

translations.literal: The trust I bear is heavy; my worry and responsibility are truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: The trust placed in me is heavy and so is my burden.

sentences.zh: 不可同于衆人，在常祀之所，必須登峰展誠，尋其靈奧。

translations.literal: I cannot be the same as the multitude, praying at the usual sacrifice site—I must climb the peak and display sincerity, seeking its numinous depths."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot pray where everyone else does. I must climb to the summit and offer my devotion where the spirit truly dwells."

sentences.zh: 」岳旣高峻，千仞壁立，岩路嶮絕，人跡罕通。

translations.literal: The peak was lofty and steep, its cliffs ten thousand feet sheer; the rock paths perilously cut off; human tracks rarely passed.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Hua rose sheer for thousands of feet, its paths nearly impassable and barely trodden by men.

sentences.zh: 武年踰六十，唯將數人，攀藤援枝，然後得上。

translations.literal: Wu was over sixty years old; taking only several men, he grasped vines and branches, and only then could ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu was past sixty. With only a few companions he hauled himself up by vines and branches until at last he reached the top.

sentences.zh: 於是稽首祈請，陳百姓懇誠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he prostrated himself in prayer, declaring the common people's earnest sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: There he kowtowed and prayed, voicing the people's desperate plea.

sentences.zh: 晚不得還，卽於岳上藉草而宿。

translations.literal: By evening he could not return, and thereupon on the peak spread grass and slept.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell before he could descend, so he slept on the mountain on a bed of grass.

sentences.zh: 夢見一白衣人來，執武手曰：「快辛苦，甚相嘉尚。

translations.literal: He dreamed a man in white came, took Wu's hand and said: "How laborious—deeply admirable."
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed that a man in white came, took his hand, and said: "What effort you have made—I honor it deeply.

sentences.zh: 」武遂驚覺，益用祗肅。

translations.literal: Wu then startled awake and redoubled reverence and solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: He started awake and prayed with even greater reverence.

sentences.zh: 至旦，雲霧四起，俄而澍雨，遠近霑洽。

translations.literal: By dawn, clouds and mist rose on four sides; soon a timely rain fell, near and far soaked through.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn clouds gathered on every side, and soon rain fell, soaking the land near and far.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，璽書勞武曰：「公年尊德重，弼諧朕躬。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu hearing of it, sent an imperial-seal letter to commend Wu, saying: "Your Lordship's years are honored and your virtue weighty; you harmonize and aid my person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuwen Yong heard of it he wrote to commend Da Xiwu: "You are aged in years and weighty in virtue, and you assist me in governing.

sentences.zh: 比以陰陽愆序，時雨不降，命公求祈，止言廟所。

translations.literal: Recently because yin and yang were out of season, timely rain did not fall, I ordered you to seek prayer—I spoke only of the temple site.
translations.idiomatic: Lately heaven and earth have been out of balance and the rains have failed. I told you only to pray at the temple below.

sentences.zh: 不謂公不憚危險，遂乃遠陟高峯。

translations.literal: I did not expect that your Lordship would not fear danger and would thereupon climb far to the high peak.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought you would ignore the danger and climb to the summit.

sentences.zh: 但神道聰明，無幽不燭，感公至誠，甘澤斯應。

translations.literal: Yet the spirit way is clear-sighted; nothing hidden escapes its illumination; moved by your Lordship's utmost sincerity, sweet moisture thus answered.
translations.idiomatic: But the spirit realm sees all, hidden or open, and answered your sincerity with rain.

sentences.zh: 聞之嘉賞，無忘于懷。

translations.literal: Hearing of it I am greatly pleased and will not forget it in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply gratified and will not forget what you have done.

sentences.zh: 今賜公雜彩百疋，公其善思嘉猷，匡朕不逮。

translations.literal: Now I grant your Lordship one hundred rolls of assorted colored silks; may your Lordship well ponder fine counsel and correct what I fall short of.
translations.idiomatic: I send you a gift of one hundred bolts of colored silks. Reflect on good counsel and help me where I fail.

sentences.zh: 念坐而論道之義，勿復更煩筋力也。」

translations.literal: Bear in mind the principle of sitting and discoursing on the Way—do not again trouble your sinews and strength."
translations.idiomatic: Remember that your place now is to counsel from your seat, not to wear yourself out on the mountain again."

sentences.zh: 震字猛略。

translations.literal: Zi Zhen, styled Menglue.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Zhen, styled Menglue.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，便騎射，走及奔馬，膂力過人。

translations.literal: From youth he was fierce and brave, skilled at riding and archery; running he could overtake a galloping horse; his physical strength surpassed ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was ferocious and brave, a natural rider and archer who on foot could keep pace with a galloping horse and whose strength outmatched ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 大統初，起家員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he first entered office as supernumerary attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he entered service as supernumerary attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗於渭北校獵，時有兔過太祖前，震與諸將競射之，馬倒而墜，震足不傾躓，因步走射之，一發中兔。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once hunted on the north bank of the Wei; at the time a hare passed before the Grand Progenitor; Zhen together with the generals raced to shoot it; his horse fell and he tumbled; Zhen's feet did not stumble; he thereupon on foot walked and shot it; with one release he hit the hare.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was hunting north of the Wei, a hare bolted past him. Zi Zhen and the other generals gave chase. His horse went down and threw him, but he kept his footing, drew his bow on foot, and dropped the hare with one shot.

sentences.zh: 顧馬纔起，遂回身騰上。

translations.literal: He looked back—the horse had just risen—he thereupon turned his body and leapt aboard.
translations.idiomatic: He glanced back as the horse was getting up, spun around, and vaulted back into the saddle.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「非此父不生此子！

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai delighted said: "Without this father, this son would not exist!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai laughed with delight: "Only this father could have such a son!"

sentences.zh: 」賜武雜彩一百段。

translations.literal: He granted Wu one hundred lengths of assorted colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Da Xiwu with one hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 十六年，封昌邑縣公，一千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was enfeoffed Duke of Changyi county, one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changyi with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 累遷撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫、通直散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was progressively transferred to general who pacifies the army, silver-gleaming blue-light grand master, unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of general who pacifies the army, silver-gleaming blue-light grand master, unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，拜儀同、〔司〕右中大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封普寧縣公。

translations.literal: At the start of Shizong, he was appointed equal-to-three-division and [Si] right center grand prefect, given the added posts of grand general of swift cavalry and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Puning county.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was given equal-to-three-division protocol and right center grand prefect, promoted to grand general of swift cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and raised to Duke of Puning.

sentences.zh: 武

translations.literal: Wu
translations.idiomatic: Wu

translations.literal: (Ping)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: cheng]

sentences.zh: 〔成〕初，進爵廣平郡公，除華州刺史。

translations.literal: [Cheng] at the start, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Guangping commandery and made governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wucheng reign he was raised to Duke of Guangping and appointed governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 震雖生自膏腴，少習武藝，然導民訓俗，頗有治方。

translations.literal: Zhen, though born from rich land, in youth practiced martial arts, yet in guiding the people and teaching custom had quite the method of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zi Zhen had been born to privilege and trained in arms from youth, he proved skilled at guiding people and shaping local custom.

sentences.zh: 秩滿還朝，為百姓所戀。

translations.literal: When his term expired he returned to court and was yearned for by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to court, the people missed him.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，大軍東討，諸將皆奔退，震與敵交戰，軍遂獨全。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, the great army campaigned east; the various generals all fled and withdrew; Zhen fought the enemy, and the army thereupon alone remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding fourth year, during the great eastern campaign, every other general fled while Zi Zhen fought on, and his army alone escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，進位大將軍，率衆征稽胡，破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, he was advanced in rank to grand general, led troops to campaign against the Ji Hu, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe first year he was made grand general, led troops against the Ji Hu, and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 建德初，襲爵鄭國公，出為金州總管、十一州九防諸軍事、金州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiande, he inherited the title Duke of Zheng state, went out as area commander of Jin Province with military affairs of eleven provinces and nine garrisons, and governor of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiande he inherited the ducal title of Zheng and was sent out as area commander of Jin Province with authority over eleven provinces and nine garrisons and as governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 四年，從高祖東伐，為前三軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed Emperor Wen east on campaign and was commander of the front third of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Emperor Wen on the eastern campaign as commander of the front third of the army.

sentences.zh: 五年，又從東伐，率步騎一萬守統軍川，攻克義寧、烏蘇二鎮，破幷州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again followed the eastern campaign, led ten thousand foot and horse to hold Tongjun River, captured the two garrisons of Yining and Wusu, and broke Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he marched east again with ten thousand foot and horse, held Tongjun River, took the garrisons of Yining and Wusu, and routed Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to upper pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 仍從平鄴，賜妾二人、女樂一部及珍玩等，拜大宗伯。

translations.literal: He still followed in pacifying Ye, was granted two concubines, one set of female musicians, and precious curios and the like, and was appointed grand master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped pacify Ye and was given two concubines, a troupe of female musicians, and fine gifts, and was made grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 震父嘗為此職，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Zhen's father had once held this office; opinion of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da Xiwu had once held that office, and contemporaries saw it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 宣政中，出為原州總管、三州二鎮諸軍事、原州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xuanzheng era, he went out as area commander of Yuan Province with military affairs of three provinces and two garrisons and governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanzheng era he was sent as area commander of Yuan with authority over three provinces and two garrisons and as governor of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 尋罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon relieved and returned home.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，薨於家。

translations.literal: At the start of Sui Kaihuang, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home early in the Kaihuang era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 震弟惎，車騎將軍、渭南縣子。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Ji was general of chariots and cavalry and Viscount of Weinan county.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Zhen's younger brother Ji was general of chariots and cavalry and Viscount of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 大象末，為益州刺史，與王謙據蜀起兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was governor of Yi Province; with Wang Qian he held Shu and raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: In late Daxiang he was governor of Yi Province and, with Wang Qian, raised troops in Shu.

sentences.zh: 尋敗，被誅。

translations.literal: Soon he was defeated and executed.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon defeated, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏文帝東討，與太尉王盟、僕射周惠達等留鎮長安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Wen of Wei campaigned east; together with Grand Commandant Wang Meng, Vice Premier Zhou Huida, and others he remained to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Wen of Wei marched east, Shun stayed in Chang'an with Grand Commandant Wang Meng, Vice Premier Zhou Huida, and others to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 時趙青雀反，盟及惠達奉魏太子出次渭北。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Qingque rebelled; Meng and Huida escorted the Wei crown prince out and encamped north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Qingque rebelled; Wang Meng and Zhou Huida took the Wei crown prince and encamped north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 順于渭橋與賊戰，頻破之，賊不敢出。

translations.literal: Shun at Weiqiao fought the bandits, repeatedly defeated them, and the bandits did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Houmo Chen Shun fought the rebels at Weiqiao, routed them again and again, and kept them bottled up.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝還，親執順手曰：「渭橋之戰，卿有殊力。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei returned, personally took Shun's hand, and said: "At the battle of Weiqiao, you had extraordinary strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen returned, he took Shun by the hand and said: "At Weiqiao you showed extraordinary force.

sentences.zh: 」便解所服金鏤玉梁帶賜之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he removed the gold-inlaid jade-bridged belt he was wearing and granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he took off his own gold-inlaid jade-bridged belt and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 南岐州氐苻安壽自號太白王，攻破武都，州郡騷動。

translations.literal: In South Qizhou the Di Fu Anshou styled himself King of Taibai, broke through Wudu, and provinces and commanderies were alarmed and stirred.
translations.idiomatic: In South Qizhou the Di chieftain Fu Anshou proclaimed himself King of Taibai, stormed Wudu, and threw the region into alarm.

sentences.zh: 復以順為大都督，往討之。

translations.literal: Shun was again made grand commander and sent to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was again made grand commander and sent to put him down.

sentences.zh: 而賊屯兵要險，軍不得進。

translations.literal: But the bandits stationed troops at strategic passes, and the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the mountain passes, and his army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 順乃設反間，離其腹心；

translations.literal: Shun thereupon set up counter-intelligence and separated their trusted inner circle;
translations.idiomatic: Shun planted disinformation and split their inner circle;

sentences.zh: 立信賞，誘其徒屬。

translations.literal: he established trust in rewards and enticed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: offered credible rewards and lured away their followers.

sentences.zh: 安壽知勢窮迫，遂率部落一千家，赴軍款附。

translations.literal: Anshou knew his situation was desperate; thereupon he led one thousand clans of his tribe to come to the army and sincerely submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshou saw he was trapped, he brought a thousand tribal households to submit.

sentences.zh: 時順弟崇又封彭城郡公，封順河間郡公。

translations.literal: At the time Shun's younger brother Chong was again enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng commandery, and Shun was enfeoffed Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: About then Shun's brother Chong was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng and Shun was made Duke of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 明年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、行西夏州事、安平郡公。

translations.literal: The next year, he was given the added posts of grand general of swift cavalry and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, acting Western Xia Province affairs, and Duke of Anping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received grand general of swift cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, acting authority over Western Xia Province, and the title Duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜大將軍，出為荊州總管、山南道五十二州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed grand general, went out as area commander of Jing Province with military affairs of fifty-two provinces on the South Mountain route, and governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand general and sent as area commander of Jing with authority over fifty-two provinces along the South Mountain route and as governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜少師，進位柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed junior preceptor and advanced in rank to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was made junior preceptor and raised to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 豆盧寧字永安，昌黎徒何人。

translations.literal: Dou Luning, styled Yong'an, was a man of Tujin in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luning, styled Yong'an, came from Tujin in Changli.

sentences.zh: 其先本姓慕容氏，前燕之支庶也。

translations.literal: His forebears originally bore the surname Murong; a cadet branch of Former Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had originally been Murong, a collateral line of Former Yan.

sentences.zh: 高祖勝，以燕。

translations.literal: A high ancestor, Sheng, with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: An early ancestor, Sheng, was associated with Yan.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，歸魏，授長樂郡守，賜姓豆盧氏，或云避難改焉。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangshi, he submitted to Wei, was granted Administrator of Changle commandery, and granted the surname Doulu; or it is said he changed it to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangshi he submitted to Wei, was made administrator of Changle, and received the surname Doulu—or so some say, taking it to escape calamity.

sentences.zh: 父長，柔玄鎮將，有威重，見稱於時。

translations.literal: His father Chang was garrison general of Rouxuan, had authority and weight, and was praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was garrison general of Rouxuan, a man of formidable repute praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 武成初，以寧著勳，追贈柱國大將軍、少保、涪陵郡公。

translations.literal: At the start of Wucheng, on account of Ning's distinguished merit, he was posthumously awarded pillar-of-state grand general, junior guardian, and Duke of Fuling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wucheng, in recognition of Dou Luning's service, his father was posthumously given pillar-of-state grand general, junior guardian, and Duke of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 寧少驍果，有志氣，身長八尺，美容儀，善騎射。

translations.literal: Ning in youth was valiant and resolute, had aspiration and spirit, stood eight chi tall, had fine bearing and appearance, and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luning was bold and spirited from youth, stood eight chi tall, cut a handsome figure, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 永安中，以別將隨爾朱天光入關，加授都督。

translations.literal: In Yong'an, as separate commander he followed Erzhu Tianguang in entering the passes and was additionally granted commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he entered the passes as a separate commander under Erzhu Tianguang and was made a commander.

sentences.zh: 又以破万俟醜奴功，賜爵靈壽縣男。

translations.literal: Again for the merit of defeating Moqi Chounu, he was granted the rank Baron of Lingshou county.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Moqi Chounu he was given the rank of Baron of Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 嘗與梁仚定遇於平涼川，相與肄射。

translations.literal: Once he met Liang Chaoding at Pingliang River, and together they practiced archery.
translations.idiomatic: He once met Liang Chaoding on the Pingliang River and they practiced archery together.

sentences.zh: 乃於百步懸莎草以射之，七發五中。

translations.literal: Thereupon at a hundred paces they suspended sedge grass to shoot at; seven shots, five hits.
translations.idiomatic: At a hundred paces they hung sedge grass as a target; Ning shot seven times and hit five.

sentences.zh: 定服其能，贈遺甚厚。

translations.literal: Chaoding admired his ability and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoding admired his skill and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 天光敗後，侯莫陳悅反，太祖討悅，寧與李弼率衆歸太祖。

translations.literal: After Tianguang was defeated, Houmochen Yue rebelled; the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Yue; Ning with Li Bi led troops to submit to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang's defeat, when Houmochen Yue rebelled, Dou Luning and Li Bi brought their forces over to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，以奉迎勳，封河陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, for the merit of welcoming him he was enfeoffed Earl of Heyang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting Emperor Xiaowu west he was enfeoffed Earl of Heyang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，除前將軍，進爵為侯，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was made front general, advanced in rank to marquis, and given an increased fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong first year he was made front general, raised to marquis, and given three hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 遷顯州刺史、顯州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Xian Province and chief arbiter of Xian Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Xian and chief arbiter of Xian.

sentences.zh: 尋拜撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，進爵為公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed general who pacifies the army and silver-gleaming blue-light grand master, advanced in rank to duke, and given an increased fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general who pacifies the army and silver-gleaming blue-light grand master, raised to duke, and given five hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 授鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was granted general who stabilizes the east and golden-purple-gleaming grand master.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posts of general who stabilizes the east and golden-purple-gleaming grand master.

sentences.zh: 從太祖擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，除武衛大將軍，兼大都督。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand Progenitor in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shaya, and was made grand general of martial guards and concurrently grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and winning at Shaya, and was made grand general of martial guards and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol and given an increased fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol and eight hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 拜北華州刺史，在州未幾，以廉平著稱。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of North Hua Province; at the province not long, on account of integrity and fairness he was famed.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of North Hua he soon won renown for integrity and fair dealing.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was given the added title attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added title of attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 七年，從于謹破稽胡帥劉平伏於上郡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he followed Yu Jin in defeating the Ji Hu chieftain Liu Pingfu at Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Yu Jin in defeating the Ji Hu chieftain Liu Pingfu at Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 及梁仚定反，以寧為軍司，監隴右諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Liang Chaoding rebelled, Ning was made army marshal and supervised all military affairs of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Chaoding rebelled, Dou Luning was made army marshal with oversight of all Longyou military affairs.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進位侍中、使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was advanced in rank to attendant-in-ordinary, commissioner bearing the staff, grand general of swift cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed he was raised to attendant-in-ordinary, commissioner bearing the staff, grand general of swift cavalry, and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 九年，從太祖迎高仲密，與東魏戰於邙山，遷左衛將軍，進爵范陽郡公，增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he followed the Grand Progenitor in welcoming Gao Zhongmi, fought Eastern Wei at Mount Mang, was transferred to left guard general, advanced in rank to Duke of Fanyang commandery, and given an increased fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to welcome Gao Zhongmi, fought Eastern Wei at Mount Mang, was made left guard general, raised to Duke of Fanyang, and given four hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 羌帥傍乞鐵

translations.literal: The Qiang chieftain Bangqi Tie
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain Bangqi Tie

translations.literal: (Hu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: cong]

sentences.zh: 〔怱〕及鄭五醜等反叛，寧率衆討平之。

translations.literal: [Cong] and Zheng Wuchou and others rebelled; Ning led troops to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi Tiecong, Zheng Wuchou, and others rebelled; Dou Luning led troops and put them down.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，改封武陽郡公，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Wuyang commandery, and he was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Wuyang and made right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 梁將王琳遣其將侯方兒、潘純陀寇江陵，寧與蔡佑、鄭永等討之，方兒等遁走。

translations.literal: Liang general Wang Lin sent his generals Hou Fanger and Pan Chuntuo to raid Jiangling; Ning with Cai You, Zheng Yong, and others campaigned against them, and Fanger and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang general Wang Lin sent Hou Fanger and Pan Chuntuo against Jiangling, Dou Luning with Cai You and Zheng Yong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 三年，武興氐及固

translations.literal: In the third year, the Wu Xing Di and Gu
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Wu Xing Di and the Gu

translations.literal: (Cha)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: dao]

sentences.zh: 〔道〕氐魏大王等，相應反叛，寧復討平之。

translations.literal: [Dao] Di Wei Dawang and others, responding together, rebelled; Ning again campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Di, Wei Dawang, and others rose together; Dou Luning put them down again.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，授柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was granted pillar-of-state grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded he was given pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 武成初，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Wucheng, he went out as governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wucheng reign he was sent out as governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 復督諸軍討稽胡郝阿保、劉桑德等，破之。

translations.literal: Again he supervised the various armies to campaign against the Ji Hu Hao Abao, Liu Sangde, and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again commanded armies against the Ji Hu chieftains Hao Abao and Liu Sangde and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遷大司寇，進封楚國公，邑萬戶，別食鹽亭縣一千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to grand minister of justice, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chu state with a fief of ten thousand households, separately sustenance of Yanting county of one thousand households, and collected its rents and levies.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made grand minister of justice, raised to Duke of Chu with a fief of ten thousand households and separate sustenance from Yanting county of one thousand households whose taxes he collected.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，授岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was granted governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding fourth year he was made governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 屬大兵東討，寧輿疾從軍。

translations.literal: It happened that the great army campaigned east; Ning, ill in his carriage, followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the great eastern campaign began, Dou Luning rode to war despite illness.

sentences.zh: 五年，薨於同州，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died at Tong Province; at the time he was sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died at Tong, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、同鄜等十州諸軍事、同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded grand guardian, military affairs of ten provinces including Tong and Fu, and governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given grand guardian, command over ten provinces including Tong and Fu, and governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 諡曰昭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhao.

sentences.zh: 初寧未有子，養弟永恩子勣。

translations.literal: Initially Ning had no son; he adopted his younger brother Yong'en's son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dou Luning had no son and adopted his brother Yong'en's son Ji.

sentences.zh: 及生子贊，親屬皆請讚為嗣。

translations.literal: When he bore a son Zan, kinsmen all asked that Zan be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: When he later had a son of his own, Zan, his relatives all urged him to make Zan heir.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也，吾何擇焉。

translations.literal: Ning said: "A brother's son is like one's own son; why should I choose between them?
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luning said: "A brother's son is as good as one's own—why should I choose?

sentences.zh: 」遂以績為世子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made Ji the heir.
translations.idiomatic: " So he kept Ji as his heir.

sentences.zh: 世以此稱之。

translations.literal: The age for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: People praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及寧薨，績襲爵，少歷顯位，大象末，上柱國、利州總管。

translations.literal: When Ning died, Ji inherited the title; in youth he passed through eminent posts; at the end of Daxiang he was upper pillar of state and area commander of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Luning died, Ji inherited the title, rose young to high office, and at the end of Daxiang was upper pillar of state and area commander of Li.

sentences.zh: 讚以寧勳，建德初，賜爵華陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Zan, on account of Ning's merit, at the start of Jiande was granted the rank Marquis of Huayang county.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, for Dou Luning's service, was made Marquis of Huayang at the start of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 累遷開府儀同大將軍、進爵武陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was progressively transferred to opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and advanced in rank to Duke of Wuyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and Duke of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 永恩少有識度，為時輩所稱。

translations.literal: Yong'en in youth had discernment and breadth and was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'en had shown judgment from youth and won praise among his peers.

sentences.zh: 初隨寧事侯莫陳悅，後與寧俱歸太祖，授殄寇將軍。

translations.literal: Initially he followed Ning in serving Houmochen Yue; afterward together with Ning he submitted to the Grand Progenitor and was granted exterminating-bandits general.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Dou Luning in serving Houmochen Yue, then came over with him to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and was made exterminating-bandits general.

sentences.zh: 以迎魏孝武功，封新興縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was enfeoffed Earl of Xinxing county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed Earl of Xinxing with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 屢逢征討，皆有功，拜龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he met campaigns; all had merit; he was appointed soaring-dragon general and palace-gentleman grand master.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in many campaigns with distinction and was made soaring-dragon general and palace-gentleman grand master.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，除直寢、右親信都督，尋轉都督，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, he was made direct attendant of the inner chamber and right trusted commander; soon he was transferred to commander and given the added post unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong eighth year he was made direct attendant of the inner chamber and right trusted commander, soon made commander, with unobstructed-direct attendant of scattered cavalry added.

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed commissioner bearing the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he received commissioner bearing the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of the deposed Emperor of Wei, he was advanced in rank to grand general of swift cavalry and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the deposed Wei emperor he was raised to grand general of swift cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為成州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he went out as governor of Cheng Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as governor of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，進爵龍

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was advanced in rank to Long
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was raised to Long

translations.literal: (Lai)
translations.idiomatic: [Zhi — completing Longzhi]

sentences.zh: 〔支〕縣侯。

translations.literal: [Zhi] county marquis.
translations.idiomatic: he was enfeoffed Marquis of Longzhi county.

sentences.zh: 三年，大將軍、安政公史寧隨突厥可汗入吐谷渾，令永恩率騎五千鎮河、鄯二州，以為邊防。

translations.literal: In the third year, Grand General, Duke of Anzheng Shi Ning followed the Turkic khan into Tuyuhun; Yong'en was ordered to lead five thousand cavalry to garrison He and Shan provinces as border defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Grand General Shi Ning, Duke of Anzheng, followed the Turkic khan into Tuyuhun; Yong'en was ordered to lead five thousand cavalry to garrison He and Shan provinces on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，授鄯州刺史，改封沃野縣公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, Yong'en was made governor of Shan Province, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Woye county, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, Yong'en was made governor of Shan Province, enfeoffed Duke of Woye county, and given an additional thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋轉隴右總管府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to chief clerk of the Longyou governor-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to chief clerk of the Longyou governor-general's office.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，遷都督利沙文三州諸軍事、利州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, he was moved to commander of military affairs in Li, Sha, and Wen provinces and governor of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng 1 (559) he was made commander of military affairs in Li, Sha, and Wen provinces and governor of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 時文州蠻叛，永恩率兵擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Man of Wen Province rebelled; Yong'en led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Man of Wen Province rebelled, Yong'en led troops and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，入為司會中大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he entered court as chief clerk of the bureau of reviews.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 1 (561) he entered court as chief clerk of the bureau of reviews.

sentences.zh: 二年，復出為隴右總管府長史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he again went out as chief clerk of the Longyou governor-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again went out as chief clerk of the Longyou governor-general's office.

sentences.zh: 寧以佐命元勳封楚國公，請以先封武陽郡三千戶益沃野之封，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Ning, as a founding merit noble enfeoffed Duke of Chu, requested that his earlier enfeoffment of Wuyang commandery, three thousand households, be added to Woye's enfeoffment; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ning, enfeoffed Duke of Chu for founding merit, asked that his earlier fief of Wuyang commandery, three thousand households, be added to Woye's enfeoffment, and the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 又增邑幷前四千五百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was again increased, together with the previous total of four thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was increased again, bringing the total to four thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官，年四十八。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office, age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈少保、幽冀等五州諸軍事、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Junior Guardian, commander of military affairs in You, Ji, and five other provinces, and governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made junior guardian, commander of military affairs in You, Ji, and five other provinces, and governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 子通嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 宇文貴字永貴，其先昌黎大棘人也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Gui, styled Yonggui, his forebears were natives of Daji in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui, styled Yonggui, came from Daji in Changli commandery.

sentences.zh: 徙居夏州。

translations.literal: The family moved and dwelt in Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: The family moved to Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 父莫豆干。

translations.literal: His father was Modugan.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Modugan.

sentences.zh: 保定中，以貴著勳，追贈柱國大將軍、少傅、夏州刺史、安平郡公。

translations.literal: In Baoding, because Gui had manifest merit, he was posthumously granted Pillar Grand General, Junior Tutor, governor of Xia Province, and Duke of Anping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding, because Yuwen Gui had won distinction, his father was posthumously made pillar grand general, junior tutor, governor of Xia Province, and duke of Anping commandery.

sentences.zh: 貴母初孕貴，夢有老人抱一兒授之曰：「賜爾是子，俾壽且貴。

translations.literal: When Gui's mother first conceived Gui, she dreamed an old man held a child and gave it to her, saying: "I grant you this child—may he live long and be noble.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Gui's mother first conceived him, she dreamed that an old man handed her a child, saying, "I give you this son—may he live long and rise high.

sentences.zh: 」及生，形類所夢，故以永貴字之。

translations.literal: " When he was born, his form resembled what she had dreamed; therefore he was given the courtesy name Yonggui.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was born he looked just as in the dream, and so he was given the courtesy name Yonggui (Ever Noble).

sentences.zh: 貴少從師受學，嘗輟書歎曰：「男兒當提劍汗馬以取公侯，何能如先生為博士也！

translations.literal: Gui in youth followed teachers in study; once he stopped reading and sighed, saying: "A man should take sword in hand and sweat on horseback to win marquisate and nobility—how can he be like a master and become a erudite!
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yuwen Gui studied with teachers, but once he laid aside his books and sighed: "A man should take sword in hand and win rank on horseback—how can he waste his life as a bookish doctor!

sentences.zh: 」正光末，破六汗拔陵圍夏州，刺史源子雍嬰城固守，以貴為統軍救之。

translations.literal: " At the end of Zhengguang, Poliuhan Baling besieged Xia Province; Governor Yuan Ziyong closed the city and held firm, making Gui commander to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of Zhengguang, Poliuhan Baling besieged Xia Province; Governor Yuan Ziyong shut the gates and held firm, appointing Gui commander to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 前後數十戰，軍中咸服其勇。

translations.literal: Before and after, in several tens of battles, the army all admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: In dozens of battles before and after, the whole army admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 後送子雍還，賊帥叱干麒麟、薛崇禮等處處屯聚，出兵邀截，貴每奮擊，輒破之。

translations.literal: Later, when Ziyong was sent back, bandit chiefs Chigan Qilin, Xue Chongli, and others gathered in camps everywhere and sent troops to intercept; Gui each time fought fiercely and always broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after escorting Ziyong back, bandit chiefs Chigan Qilin, Xue Chongli, and others had camps everywhere and sent troops to intercept; Gui fought hard each time and always routed them.

sentences.zh: 除武騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Palace Horseman.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular palace horseman.

sentences.zh: 又從子雍討葛榮，軍敗奔鄴，為榮所圍。

translations.literal: Again he followed Ziyong to campaign against Ge Rong; the army was defeated and fled to Ye, and was surrounded by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Ziyong against Ge Rong; the army was beaten, fled to Ye, and was surrounded by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 賊屢來攻，貴每縋而出戰，賊莫敢當其鋒。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly came to attack; Gui each time was lowered by rope to go out and fight, and the bandits did not dare meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked again and again; each time Gui was lowered by rope to sally forth, and none dared meet his charge.

sentences.zh: 然凶徒寔繁，圍久不解。

translations.literal: Yet the wicked masses were truly numerous, and the siege long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: But the enemy host was vast, and the siege dragged on without end.

sentences.zh: 貴乃於地道潛出，北見爾朱榮，陳賊兵勢，榮深納之。

translations.literal: Gui then secretly went out through a tunnel, went north and saw Erzhu Rong, and set forth the bandits' military strength; Rong deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then slipped out through a tunnel, went north to Erzhu Rong, and reported the rebels' strength; Rong took his counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 因從榮擒葛榮於滏口，加別將。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Rong and captured Ge Rong at Fekou; he was promoted to separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Rong and captured Ge Rong at Fekou and was promoted to separate commander.

sentences.zh: 又從元天穆平邢杲，轉都督。

translations.literal: Again he followed Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao and was transferred to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao and was made commander.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，貴率鄉兵從爾朱榮焚河橋，力戰有功。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Gui led local troops with Erzhu Rong to burn the river bridge and fought hard with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Gui led local troops with Erzhu Rong to burn the river bridge and fought with great merit.

sentences.zh: 加征虜將軍，封革融縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was further made General Who Subdues Captives, enfeoffed Marquis of Gerong county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made general who subdues captives and enfeoffed Marquis of Gerong with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除郢州刺史，入為武衛將軍、

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Ying Province and entered court as Martial Guard General and
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Ying Province and entered court as martial guard general and

translations.literal: (Guan)
translations.idiomatic: [Ge — completing within-the-palace]

sentences.zh: 〔閤〕內大都督。

translations.literal: [Ge] inner grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: grand commander within the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷，進爵化政郡公。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the western move, he was advanced to Duke of Huazheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the move west, he was promoted to Duke of Huazheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 大統初，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong, he was moved to Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was made right guard general.

sentences.zh: 貴善騎射，有將率才。

translations.literal: Gui was skilled at mounted archery and had the talent of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui was skilled at mounted archery and had true command talent.

sentences.zh: 太祖又以宗室，甚親委之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also, because he was of the imperial clan, greatly favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also favored and trusted him deeply as a kinsman of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 三年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was advanced to Chariots-and-Cavalry Grand General and Commissioner with Ceremonial Status Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to chariots-and-cavalry grand general and commissioner with ceremonial status equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 與獨孤信入洛陽。

translations.literal: Together with Dugu Xin he entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang together with Dugu Xin.

sentences.zh: 東魏潁州

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Ying Province
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Ying Province

translations.literal: (Ci)
translations.idiomatic: [Zhang — completing chief clerk]

sentences.zh: 〔長〕史賀若統據潁川來降，東魏遣其將堯雄、趙育、是云寶率衆二萬攻潁。

translations.literal: [Zhang] chief clerk He Ruotong held Yingchuan and came to surrender; Eastern Wei sent its generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao leading twenty thousand men to attack Ying.
translations.idiomatic: chief clerk He Ruotong held Yingchuan and surrendered; Eastern Wei sent generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao with twenty thousand men to attack Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 貴自洛陽率步騎二千救之，軍次陽翟。

translations.literal: Gui from Luoyang led two thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue it; the army halted at Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui led two thousand foot and horse from Luoyang to relieve the city and halted at Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 雄等已度馬橋，去潁川三十里，東魏行臺任祥又率衆四萬餘，與雄合。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others had already crossed Ma Bridge, thirty li from Yingchuan; Eastern Wei Mobile Headquarters Ren Xiang also led more than forty thousand men and joined Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others had already crossed Ma Bridge, thirty li from Yingchuan; Eastern Wei mobile headquarters commander Ren Xiang also brought more than forty thousand men to join Xiong.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸以彼衆我寡，不可爭鋒。

translations.literal: The generals all thought the enemy many and themselves few, and that they could not contend at the edge.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals all said the enemy outnumbered them and they should not give battle.

sentences.zh: 貴曰：「兵機倚伏，固不可以常理論。

translations.literal: Gui said: "The opportunity of war rests on shifting fortune—it truly cannot be judged by ordinary reason.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said: "The turns of war cannot be judged by ordinary reckoning.

sentences.zh: 古人能以寡制衆者，皆由預睹成敗，決必然之策耳。

translations.literal: Those ancients who could use the few to control the many all did so by foreseeing success and failure and deciding on a strategy that must prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who beat larger forces always foresaw the outcome and chose a plan that had to succeed.

sentences.zh: 吾雖闇於成事，然謂進與賀若合勢，為計之上者。

translations.literal: Though I am dull about completed affairs, still I say that advancing to join forces with He Ruo is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: I may be no strategist, but I say advancing to join He Ruotong is our best course.

sentences.zh: 請為諸軍說之。

translations.literal: Allow me to explain it for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Let me explain it for all of you.

sentences.zh: 堯雄等必以為潁川孤危，勢非其敵，又謂吾寡弱獨進，若悉力以攻潁，必指掌可破。

translations.literal: Yao Xiong and the others will surely think Yingchuan isolated and perilous, its strength not their match, and also think that we are few and weak and advancing alone; if they use all their strength to attack Ying, it can surely be broken as easily as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiong and the others will think Yingchuan isolated and helpless, and that we are a small force advancing alone; if they throw everything at Ying, they will take it at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 旣陷潁川，便與任祥軍合，同惡相濟，為害更甚。

translations.literal: Once Yingchuan falls, they will join Ren Xiang's army; like-minded evils aiding one another—the harm will be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yingchuan falls they will unite with Ren Xiang's army, and the combined threat will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 吾今屯兵陽翟，便是入其數內。

translations.literal: We now station troops at Yangdi—that is already within their count.
translations.idiomatic: By halting at Yangdi we are already counted among the doomed.

sentences.zh: 若賀若一陷，吾輩坐此何為。

translations.literal: If He Ruo falls, what are we sitting here for?
translations.idiomatic: If He Ruotong falls, what good are we doing here?

sentences.zh: 進據潁川，有城可守。

translations.literal: Advance and hold Yingchuan—there is a city that can be defended.
translations.idiomatic: Advance into Yingchuan and we have walls to hold.

sentences.zh: 雄見吾入城，出其不意，進則狐疑，退則不可。

translations.literal: When Xiong sees us enter the city, taken by surprise, if he advances he will be doubtful, and if he retreats he cannot.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong sees us inside the city he will be caught off guard—advancing, he will hesitate; retreating, he cannot.

sentences.zh: 然後與諸軍盡力擊之，何往不克。

translations.literal: Then together with the armies we will exert full strength to strike them—where would we not conquer?
translations.idiomatic: Then we and the other armies can strike with full force—where would we fail?

sentences.zh: 願勿疑也。

translations.literal: I beg you not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Do not doubt it.

sentences.zh: 」遂入潁川。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he entered Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he entered Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 雄等稍前，貴率千人背城為陳，與雄合戰，貴馬中流矢，乃短兵步鬬。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others advanced slightly; Gui led a thousand men with their backs to the wall to form ranks and joined battle with Xiong; Gui's horse was struck by a flying arrow, and he then fought at close quarters on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others pressed forward; Gui led a thousand men with their backs to the wall and met Xiong in battle; when his horse was hit by an arrow he fought on foot at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 士衆用命。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers exerted their orders.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought with all their might.

sentences.zh: 雄大敗輕走，趙育于陳降，獲其輜重，俘萬餘人，盡放令還。

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly defeated and fled lightly; Zhao Yu surrendered on the field; they captured his baggage train, took more than ten thousand prisoners, and entirely released them to return.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was routed and fled; Zhao Yu surrendered on the field; they captured the baggage train and more than ten thousand prisoners, then released them all.

sentences.zh: 任祥聞雄敗，遂不敢進。

translations.literal: Ren Xiang heard Xiong was defeated and therefore did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Xiang heard that Xiong had been beaten, he did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 尋而儀同怡峰率騎五百赴貴，貴乘勝逼祥。

translations.literal: Soon Commissioner Yi Feng led five hundred cavalry to join Gui; Gui pressed the victory and drove on Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Commissioner Yi Feng arrived with five hundred cavalry; Gui pressed the victory and drove on Xiang.

sentences.zh: 祥退保宛陵，追及之。

translations.literal: Xiang retreated to hold Wancheng; they pursued and caught him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang fell back to Wancheng; they pursued and caught up with him.

sentences.zh: 會日暝，結陳相持。

translations.literal: It happened that the day grew dark; they formed ranks and faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell and the two sides formed ranks and faced each other.

sentences.zh: 明旦合戰，俘斬甚多。

translations.literal: At dawn they joined battle; captives and heads taken were very many.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought again and took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 祥軍旣敗，是云寶亦降。

translations.literal: Once Xiang's army was defeated, Shiyun Bao also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang's army was broken, Shiyun Bao surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 師還。

translations.literal: The army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army then returned.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝在天遊園，以金巵置侯上，命公卿射中者，卽以賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei was at the Tianyou Garden; he placed a golden goblet on the marquis's head and ordered the nobles and ministers that whoever shot and hit it would at once be given it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei was at the Tianyou Garden; he set a golden goblet on a marquis's head and told the nobles and ministers that whoever hit it with an arrow would receive it.

sentences.zh: 貴一發而中。

translations.literal: Gui with one shot hit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui hit it with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「由基之妙，正當爾耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: "Yang Youji's skill—just like this indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "The art of Yang Youji—just like this!

sentences.zh: 」進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to Palace Attendant, Grand General of Flying Cavalry, and Opening-the-Feudatory Commissioner with Ceremonial Status Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to palace attendant, grand general of flying cavalry, and opening-the-feudatory commissioner with ceremonial status equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 歷夏岐二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as governor of Xia and Qi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Xia and Qi provinces.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷中外府左長史，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was moved to left chief clerk of the central-and-outer office and advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made left chief clerk of the central-and-outer office and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁彌定為宗人獠甘所逐，來奔。

translations.literal: Tanchang King Liang Miding was driven out by his clansman Liao Gan and came in flight to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tanchang King Liang Miding was driven out by his clansman Liao Gan and fled to surrender.

sentences.zh: 又有羌酋傍乞鐵怱因梁仚定反後，據有渠株川，擁種類數千家，與渭州民鄭五醜扇惑諸羌同反，憑險置柵者十餘所。

translations.literal: There was also the Qiang chieftain Bangqi Tiecong, who after Liang Xianding's rebellion held Quzhu River, gathered several thousand of his kind, and with Zheng Wuchou of Wei Province incited the various Qiang to rebel together; relying on steep terrain they set up more than ten stockades.
