translations.idiomatic: There was also the Qiang chieftain Bangqi Tiecong, who after Liang Xianding's rebellion held Quzhu River, gathered several thousand tribesmen, and with Zheng Wuchou of Wei Province stirred the Qiang to rebel; they fortified more than ten stockades in rugged country.

sentences.zh: 太祖令貴與豆盧寧、史寧討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Gui together with Doulu Ning and Shi Ning to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Yuwen Gui, Doulu Ning, and Shi Ning to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 貴等擒斬鐵怱及五醜。

translations.literal: Gui and the others captured and beheaded Tiecong and Wuchou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and the others captured and beheaded Tiecong and Wuchou.

sentences.zh: 史寧又別擊獠甘，破之，乃納彌定。

translations.literal: Shi Ning separately attacked Liao Gan, defeated him, and then received Miding.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning separately attacked Liao Gan, defeated him, and then installed Miding.

sentences.zh: 並於渠株川置岷州。

translations.literal: They also established Min Province at Quzhu River.
translations.idiomatic: They also established Min Province at Quzhu River.

sentences.zh: 朝廷美其功，遂於粟坂立碑，以紀其績。

translations.literal: The court praised their merit and therefore set up a stele at Suban to record their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised their achievement and erected a stele at Suban to record it.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, he went out as governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he went out as governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 二年，授大都督、興西蓋等六州諸軍事、興州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was granted Grand Commander, commander of military affairs in Xing, Xi, Gai, and six other provinces, and governor of Xing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made grand commander, commander of military affairs in Xing, Xi, Gai, and six other provinces, and governor of Xing Province.

sentences.zh: 先是興州氐反，自貴至州，人情稍定。

translations.literal: Earlier the Di of Xing Province had rebelled; from the time Gui reached the province, popular sentiment gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Xing Province had rebelled earlier; once Gui reached the province, the people gradually calmed.

sentences.zh: 貴表請于梁州置屯田，數州豐足。

translations.literal: Gui memorialized requesting garrison agriculture be established at Liang Province; several provinces became abundant and sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Gui memorialized to establish garrison farms in Liang Province, and several provinces grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔貴代尉遲迥鎮蜀。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered Gui to replace Yuchi Jiong in garrisoning Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ordered Gui to replace Yuchi Jiong as garrison commander in Shu.

sentences.zh: 時隆州人開府李光賜反於鹽亭，與其黨帛玉成、寇食堂、譙淹、蒲皓、馬術等攻圍隆州。

translations.literal: At that time Li Guangci of Long Province, an opening-the-feudatory officer, rebelled at Yanting with his partisans Bo Yucheng, Kou Shitang, Qiao Yan, Pu Hao, Ma Shu, and others and attacked and besieged Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Guangci of Long Province, an opening-the-feudatory officer, rebelled at Yanting with his followers Bo Yucheng, Kou Shitang, Qiao Yan, Pu Hao, Ma Shu, and others and besieged Long Province.

sentences.zh: 州人李祏亦聚衆反，開府張遁舉兵應之。

translations.literal: Li Zhi of the province also gathered a crowd in rebellion; Opening-the-Feudatory Zhang Dun raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi of the province also raised a rebel band; Opening-the-Feudatory Zhang Dun took up arms in support.

sentences.zh: 貴乃命開府叱奴興救隆州，又令開府成亞擊祏及遁。

translations.literal: Gui then ordered Opening-the-Feudatory Chinu Xing to rescue Long Province, and also ordered Opening-the-Feudatory Cheng Ya to strike Zhi and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then ordered Opening-the-Feudatory Chinu Xing to relieve Long Province and Opening-the-Feudatory Cheng Ya to attack Zhi and Dun.

sentences.zh: 勢蹙遂降，執送京師。

translations.literal: Their strength was pressed tight and they thereupon surrendered; they were seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, they surrendered and were sent to the capital as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 除都督益潼等八州諸軍事、益州刺史，就加小司徒。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of military affairs in Yi, Tong, and eight other provinces and governor of Yi Province, and at the same time was further made Junior Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of military affairs in Yi, Tong, and eight other provinces and governor of Yi Province, and at the same time promoted to junior minister of education.

sentences.zh: 先是蜀人多刼盜，貴乃召任俠傑健者，署為遊軍二十四部，令其督捕，由是頗息。

translations.literal: Earlier the people of Shu were much given to robbery; Gui then summoned bold and able men of chivalry, appointed them to twenty-four roaming-army sections, and ordered them to supervise capture—thereby the trouble largely ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long been troubled by banditry; Gui recruited bold and able men, organized them into twenty-four roaming-army sections to hunt down robbers, and the plague largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位柱國，拜御正中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, Gui was advanced to Pillar of State and appointed Chief Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, Gui was promoted to pillar of state and made chief director of imperial clan affairs.

sentences.zh: 武成初，與賀蘭祥討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: At the start of Wucheng, together with Helan Xiang he campaigned against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wucheng he campaigned against Tuyuhun together with Helan Xiang.

sentences.zh: 軍還，進封許國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to Duke of Xu state with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was promoted to Duke of Xu with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 舊爵廻封一子。

translations.literal: His old title was transferred to enfeoff one son.
translations.idiomatic: His former title was transferred to enfeoff one son.

sentences.zh: 遷大司空，治小冢宰，歷大司徒，遷太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand minister of works, served as junior director of the grand steward, passed through grand minister of education, and was transferred to grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand minister of works, served as junior director of the grand steward, then grand minister of education, and finally grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 貴好音樂，耽弈碁，留連不倦。

translations.literal: Gui loved music, was addicted to weiqi, and lingered over them without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wengui loved music and chess and could lose himself in them for hours.

sentences.zh: 然好施愛士，時人頗以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he loved to give and cherish men of talent; people of the time quite praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was generous and fond of nurturing talent, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 保定之末，使突厥迎皇后。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoding, he was sent with the Turks to welcome the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Baoding (561–565), he was sent with the Turks to escort the empress home.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，還至張掖，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, on returning to Zhangye, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe (568), he died on the road back at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed grand tutor; posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor and given the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 子善嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歷位開府儀同三司、大將軍、柱國、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of privilege to open an office equal to three ministers, grand general, pillar-of-state, and governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to privilege equal to three ministers, grand general, pillar-of-state, and governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 以罪免，尋復本官，除大宗伯。

translations.literal: Removed from office for a crime, he soon recovered his original post and was appointed grand director of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed for a crime, he was soon restored to his former rank and appointed grand director of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 大象末，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was advanced to upper pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang (581), he was promoted to upper pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 善弟忻，少以父軍功賜爵化政郡公。

translations.literal: Shan's younger brother Xin, in youth because of his father's military merit was granted the title Marquis of Huazheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's younger brother Xin received the title marquis of Huazheng commandery in youth for their father's military service.

sentences.zh: 驍勇絕倫，有將帥才略。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave beyond compare, he had the talent and strategy of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fearless and unmatched in valor, he had a commander's talent and strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至上柱國，進封英國公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the rank of upper pillar-of-state and was advanced to Duke of Ying State.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang he became an upper pillar-of-state and was enfeoffed duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 忻弟愷，少好學，頗解屬文，雜藝多通，尤精巧思。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Kai, in youth loved learning, was quite skilled at literary composition, broadly mastered many arts, and was especially ingenious in design.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Kai loved learning from youth, wrote competently, mastered many arts, and was especially clever with design.

sentences.zh: 亦以父軍功賜爵雙泉縣伯。

translations.literal: He too because of his father's military merit was granted the title Baron of Shuangquan county.
translations.idiomatic: He too received the title baron of Shuangquan county for their father's military service.

sentences.zh: 尋襲祖爵安平郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he inherited his grandfather's title Duke of Anping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inherited his grandfather's title, duke of Anping commandery.

sentences.zh: 起家右侍上士，稍遷御正中大夫。

translations.literal: He began his career as right attendant upper gentleman and was gradually promoted to chief director of the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a right-attendant upper gentleman and rose to chief director of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 保定中，位至上開府。

translations.literal: During Baoding, he reached the rank of upper privilege to open an office.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding he attained the rank of upper privilege to open a government office.

sentences.zh: 是云寶、趙育旣至，初並拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Shiyun Bao and Zhao Yu arrived, at first both were appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and privilege equal to three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiyun Bao and Zhao Yu came to court, both were first made grand generals of chariots and cavalry with privilege equal to three ministers.

sentences.zh: 寶後累遷至大將軍、都督涼甘瓜州諸軍、涼州刺史，賜爵洞城郡公。

translations.literal: Bao afterward was repeatedly promoted to grand general, commander of all military affairs of Liang, Gan, and Gua provinces, and governor of Liang Province, and was granted the title Duke of Dongcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was later promoted to grand general, commander of Liang, Gan, and Gua provinces, and governor of Liang Province, and enfeoffed duke of Dongcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，吐谷渾侵逼涼州，寶與戰不利，遂歿於陣。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizong's reign, Tuyuhun pressed Liang Province; Bao fought unfavorably and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's reign, when Tuyuhun threatened Liang Province, Bao was defeated and killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 楊忠，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Zhong was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 小名奴奴。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Nunu.
translations.idiomatic: His childhood name was Nunu.

sentences.zh: 高祖元壽，魏初，為武川鎮司馬，因家於神武樹頹焉。

translations.literal: High ancestor Yuanshou, in the early Wei, was marshal of Wuchuan garrison and thereupon made his home at Shenwu Shuitui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuanshou, in early Wei times, was marshal of Wuchuan garrison and settled the family at Shenwu Shuitui.

sentences.zh: 祖烈，龍驤將軍、太原郡守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Lie, dragon-charger general and prefect of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lie was dragon-charger general and prefect of Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父禎，以軍功除建遠將軍。

translations.literal: Father Zhen, because of military merit was appointed distant-campaign general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen became distant-campaign general for military merit.

sentences.zh: 屬魏末喪亂，避地中山，結義徒以討鮮于脩禮，遂死之。

translations.literal: At the time of Wei's end and disorder, he fled to Zhongshan, gathered righteous followers to attack Xianyu Xiuli, and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the chaos at the end of Wei he took refuge at Zhongshan, raised a band of volunteers against Xianyu Xiuli, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 保定中，以忠勳，追贈柱國大將軍，少保、興城郡公。

translations.literal: During Baoding, because of Zhong's merit, posthumously enfeoffed pillar-of-state and grand general, junior tutor, and Duke of Xingcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding, in recognition of Yang Zhong's service, his father was posthumously made pillar-of-state and grand general, junior tutor, and duke of Xingcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 忠美髭髯，身長七尺八寸，狀貌瓌偉，武藝絕倫，識量沉深，有將帥之略。

translations.literal: Zhong had a fine beard and moustache, stood seven feet eight inches, was imposing in appearance, unmatched in martial skill, deep in judgment and capacity, and had a commander's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong had a fine beard, stood seven feet eight inches tall, looked imposing, was unmatched in arms, and combined deep judgment with a commander's strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 年十八，客游泰山。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, he traveled as a guest to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was traveling as a guest on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 會梁兵攻郡，陷之，遂被執至江左。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang troops attacked the commandery, took it, and he was thereupon captured and taken to the lands east of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces attacked and captured the commandery, he was taken prisoner to the south.

sentences.zh: 在梁五年，從北海王顥入洛，除直閤將軍。

translations.literal: In Liang five years, he followed Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao into Luoyang and was appointed straight-gate general.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in Liang he followed Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao into Luoyang and was made straight-gate general.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，爾朱度律召為帳下統軍。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Erzhu Dulü summoned him as commander under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Erzhu Dulü took him onto his staff as a banner commander.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱兆以輕騎自幷州入洛陽，忠時預焉。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao with light cavalry entered Luoyang from Bing Province, Zhong was then present.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao rode into Luoyang from Bing Province with light cavalry, Yang Zhong was with him.

sentences.zh: 賜爵昌縣伯，拜都督，又別封小黃縣伯。

translations.literal: Granted the title Baron of Chang county, appointed commander; also separately enfeoffed Baron of Xiaohuang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Chang county and made commander, and also received a separate fief as baron of Xiaohuang county.

sentences.zh: 從獨孤信破梁下溠戍，平南陽，並有功。

translations.literal: He followed Dugu Xin in breaking Liang's Xiazhao garrison and pacifying Nanyang, both with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dugu Xin in taking Liang's Xiazhao garrison and pacifying Nanyang, winning merit in both.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武舉兵內侮，忠時隨信在洛，遂從魏孝武西遷，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu raised troops to insult within, Zhong then followed Xin at Luoyang and thereupon followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration, advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched south against the court, Yang Zhong was with Dugu Xin at Luoyang and followed Emperor Xiaowu west, being promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 仍從平潼關，破回洛城。

translations.literal: Still he followed in pacifying Tong Pass and breaking Huiluo city.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in pacifying Tong Pass and capturing Huiluo city.

sentences.zh: 除安西將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Appointed general who pacifies the west and grand master with silver seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the west and grand master with silver seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 東魏荊州刺史辛纂據穰城，忠從獨孤信討之，纂戰敗退走。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's governor of Jing Province Xin Zuan held Xiang city; Zhong followed Dugu Xin to attack him, and Zuan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei's governor of Jing Province, Xin Zuan, held Xiang city, Yang Zhong followed Dugu Xin against him; Zuan was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 信令忠與都督康洛兒、元長生為前驅，馳至其城，叱門者曰：「今大軍已至，城中有應，爾等求活，何不避走！

translations.literal: Xin ordered Zhong with commanders Kang Luo'er and Yuan Changsheng as vanguard; they galloped to the city and shouted at the gatekeepers: "Now the great army has arrived, there are men within the city who will respond—if you seek to live, why not flee and save yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin sent Yang Zhong with commanders Kang Luo'er and Yuan Changsheng as vanguard; they galloped to the walls and shouted at the gatekeepers: "The main army is here and men inside will open the gates—if you want to live, why not run!"

sentences.zh: 」門者盡散。

translations.literal: " The gatekeepers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " The gatekeepers all fled.

sentences.zh: 忠與洛兒、長生乘城而入，彎弓大呼，纂兵衛百余人莫之敢禦，斬纂以徇，城中懾服。

translations.literal: Zhong with Luo'er and Changsheng rode up into the city, bent the bow and shouted loudly; Zuan's guards of more than a hundred men none dared resist, beheaded Zuan to display, and the city submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong, Luo'er, and Changsheng rode into the city, drew their bows, and shouted; none of Xin Zuan's hundred-odd guards dared resist. They beheaded Zuan as a warning and the city submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，以東魏之逼，與信奔梁。

translations.literal: After half a year, because of Eastern Wei's pressure, he fled with Xin to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year, pressed by Eastern Wei, he fled with Dugu Xin to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝深奇之，以為

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly marveled at him and made him
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was deeply impressed and made him

translations.literal: (Da)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: 大]

sentences.zh: 〔文〕德主帥、關外侯。

translations.literal: [Wen] commander-in-chief of virtue, Marquis Outside the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: commander-in-chief of Wende virtue and marquis outside the pass. [variant: 文 vs 大]

sentences.zh: 大統三年，與信俱歸闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he returned to court together with Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537), he returned to court with Dugu Xin.

sentences.zh: 太祖召居帳下。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor summoned him to dwell under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai brought him into his personal following.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖狩於龍門，忠獨當一猛獸，左挾其腰，右拔其舌。

translations.literal: Once when following the Grand Progenitor hunting at Longmen, Zhong alone faced down a fierce beast, with his left hand gripping its waist and his right hand pulling out its tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt at Longmen with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, Yang Zhong alone faced a fierce beast, gripped its waist with his left hand, and pulled out its tongue with his right.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 北臺謂猛獸為「揜于」，因以字之。

translations.literal: The northern platform called fierce beasts "yanzi," and so gave him that as his style.
translations.idiomatic: The northern court called such beasts "yanzi," and gave him that word as his style name.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，破沙苑。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai and breaking Sha Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai and winning the battle of Sha Garden.

sentences.zh: 遷征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫，進爵襄城縣公。

translations.literal: Transferred to general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon; advanced in rank to Duke of Xiangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, and promoted to duke of Xiangcheng county.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，忠與壯士五人力戰守橋，敵人遂不敢進。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Zhong with five stalwart men fought hard to hold the bridge, and the enemy thereupon did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao, Yang Zhong and five picked men fought desperately to hold the bridge, and the enemy dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 以功除左光祿大夫、雲州刺史，兼大都督。

translations.literal: For merit appointed grand master with left seal and purple ribbon and governor of Yun Province, concurrently great governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made grand master with left seal and purple ribbon and governor of Yun Province, with concurrent rank as great governor-general.

sentences.zh: 又與李遠破黑水稽胡，並與怡峰解玉壁圍，轉洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Again with Li Yuan he broke the Black Water Jiehu, and together with Yi Feng relieved the siege of Yubi, then was transferred to governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Li Yuan in defeating the Black Water Jiehu, and with Yi Feng lifted the siege of Yubi before being transferred to governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 邙山之戰，先登陷陳。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, he was first to ascend and break the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang he was first over the wall and broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 除大都督，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Appointed great governor-general; advanced to grand general of chariots and cavalry, privilege equal to three ministers, and attendant at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made great governor-general and promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry with privilege equal to three ministers and attendant at the gate.

sentences.zh: 追封母蓋氏為北海郡君。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed his mother Lady Gai as Lady of Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Gai, was posthumously enfeoffed lady of Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋除都督朔燕顯蔚四州諸軍事、朔州刺史，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon appointed commander of all military affairs of Shu, Yan, Xian, and Wei four provinces and governor of Shu Province; added attendant within the palace, grand general of agile cavalry, and privilege to open an office equal to three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of Shu, Yan, Xian, and Wei provinces and governor of Shu Province, and also given attendant within the palace, grand general of agile cavalry, and privilege to open an office equal to three ministers.

sentences.zh: 及東魏圍潁川，蠻帥

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan, the barbarian chief
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan, the barbarian chief

translations.literal: (Ri)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: 日]

sentences.zh: 〔田〕柱清據險為亂，忠率兵討平之。

translations.literal: [Tian] Zhuqing held perilous ground in rebellion; Zhong led troops to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhuqing seized rugged terrain and rebelled; Yang Zhong led troops and put down the revolt. [variant: 田 vs 日]

sentences.zh: 時侯景渡江，梁武喪敗，其西義陽郡守馬伯符以下溠城降。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze; Emperor Wu of Liang suffered defeat, and his western Yiyang commandery prefect Ma Bofu below Xiazhao city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and Emperor Wu of Liang was defeated, Ma Bofu, Liang prefect of Yiyang, surrendered Xiazhao city.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因之，將經略漢、沔，乃授忠都督三荊二襄二廣南雍平信隨江二郢淅十五州諸軍事，鎮穰城。

translations.literal: The court took advantage of this and planned to extend control over Han and Mian; thereupon Zhong was appointed commander of all military affairs of fifteen provinces—three Jing, two Xiang, two Guang, southern Yong, Ping, Xin, Sui, Jiang, two Ying, and Xi—and stationed at Xiang city.
translations.idiomatic: The court seized the moment to push into the Han and Mian region and made Yang Zhong commander of fifteen provinces, stationing him at Xiang city.

sentences.zh: 以伯符為鄉導，攻梁齊興郡及昌州，皆克之。

translations.literal: Using Bofu as guide, he attacked Liang's Qixing commandery and Chang Province, and both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: With Bofu as guide he attacked Liang's Qixing commandery and Chang Province and captured both.

sentences.zh: 梁雍州刺史、岳陽王蕭詧雖稱藩附，而尚有貳心。

translations.literal: Liang's governor of Yong Province, Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha, though he declared himself a vassal and submitted, still harbored a divided heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha, Liang prince of Yueyang and governor of Yong Province, had submitted as a vassal but still wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忠自樊城觀兵於漢濱，易旗遞進，實騎二千，詧登樓望之，以為三萬也，懼而服焉。

translations.literal: Zhong from Fancheng reviewed troops on the Han shore, changing banners in relay; in fact there were two thousand horsemen, but when Cha ascended a tower to look, he thought there were thirty thousand, and in fear submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From Fancheng Yang Zhong paraded along the Han with banners changing in relay; he had only two thousand horsemen, but Xiao Cha, watching from a tower, took them for thirty thousand and submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 梁司州刺史柳仲禮留其長史馬岫守安陸，自率兵騎一萬寇襄陽。

translations.literal: Liang's governor of Si Province Liu Zhongli left his chief clerk Ma Xiu to hold Anlu and himself led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to raid Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli, Liang governor of Si Province, left his chief clerk Ma Xiu to hold Anlu and led ten thousand men to raid Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 初，梁竟陵郡守孫暠以其郡來附，太祖命大都督符貴往鎮之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang's prefect of Jingling commandery Sun Gao had brought his commandery to submit; the Grand Progenitor ordered great governor-general Fu Gui to go and garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Gao, Liang prefect of Jingling, had surrendered his commandery, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent great governor-general Fu Gui to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 及仲禮至，暠乃執貴以降。

translations.literal: When Zhongli arrived, Gao thereupon seized Gui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli arrived, Sun Gao seized Fu Gui and went over to him.

sentences.zh: 仲禮又進遣其將王叔孫與暠同守。

translations.literal: Zhongli further sent forward his general Wang Shusun to hold it together with Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli then sent his general Wang Shusun to hold Jingling with Sun Gao.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，乃令忠帥衆南伐。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was angered and thereupon ordered Zhong to lead the host south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was furious and ordered Yang Zhong south with an army.

sentences.zh: 攻梁隨郡，克之，獲其守將桓和。

translations.literal: He attacked Liang's Sui commandery, took it, and captured its defending general Huan He.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Liang's Sui commandery, captured it, and took its defender Huan He prisoner.

sentences.zh: 所過城戍，望風請服。

translations.literal: Every walled post he passed submitted at the sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Every fort along the route surrendered at his approach.

sentences.zh: 忠乃進圍安陸。

translations.literal: Zhong thereupon advanced to besiege Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong then pressed on to besiege Anlu.

sentences.zh: 仲禮聞隨郡陷，恐安陸不守，遂馳歸赴援。

translations.literal: Zhongli heard that Sui commandery had fallen, feared Anlu could not be held, and thereupon galloped back to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli learned that Sui had fallen, fearing Anlu could not hold he raced back to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 諸將恐仲禮至則安陸難下，請急攻之。

translations.literal: The generals feared that if Zhongli arrived Anlu would be hard to take and asked to attack it urgently.
translations.idiomatic: His officers feared that once Zhongli arrived Anlu would be impossible to take and urged an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「攻守勢殊，未可卒拔。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Attack and defense differ in advantage; it cannot be suddenly pulled down.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong said: "Attack and defense are not the same game—we cannot storm it at once.

sentences.zh: 若引日勞師，表裏受敵，非計也。

translations.literal: If we draw out days and weary the army, we shall be attacked inside and out—this is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we linger and wear down our troops, we will be caught between the city and Zhongli's relief force—that is no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 南人多習水軍，不閑野戰。

translations.literal: Southerners mostly are practiced in river warfare and are not skilled in field battle.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners are used to fighting on water, not in open field battle.

sentences.zh: 仲禮回師在近路，吾出其不意，以奇兵襲之，彼怠我奮，一舉必克，則安陸不攻自拔，諸城可傳檄而定也。

translations.literal: Zhongli is turning back on the near road; if we strike him by surprise with a special force, they weary and we are eager—one blow will surely take him, then Anlu will fall without attack and the other cities can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli is coming back by the nearest road; if we hit him unexpectedly with a picked force, his men will be tired and ours fresh—we can crush him in one stroke, and Anlu will fall without a siege while the rest of the cities can be won by dispatch alone."

sentences.zh: 」於是選騎二千，銜枚夜進，遇仲禮於淙頭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he selected two thousand horsemen, marched at night with gags in their mouths, and met Zhongli at Chongtou.
translations.idiomatic: He chose two thousand horsemen, marched silently by night, and met Liu Zhongli at Chongtou.

sentences.zh: 忠親自陷陳，擒仲禮，悉俘其衆。

translations.literal: Zhong personally broke the enemy line, captured Zhongli, and took all his men prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong himself broke the line, captured Liu Zhongli, and took his entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 馬岫以安陸降，王叔孫斬孫暠，以竟陵降，皆如忠所策。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu surrendered Anlu; Wang Shusun beheaded Sun Gao and surrendered Jingling—all just as Zhong had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu surrendered Anlu; Wang Shusun killed Sun Gao and surrendered Jingling—just as Yang Zhong had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝遣使送子方畧為質，幷送載書，請魏以石城為限，梁以安陸為界。

translations.literal: Liang's Emperor Yuan Di sent envoys offering his son Fanglue as hostage and also sent a written covenant, asking that Wei take Shicheng as its limit and Liang take Anlu as its boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan Di of Liang sent envoys offering his son Fanglue as hostage and a written covenant proposing Shicheng as Wei's border and Anlu as Liang's.

sentences.zh: 乃旋師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 進爵陳留郡公。

translations.literal: Advanced in rank to Duke of Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to duke of Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 十七年，梁元帝逼其兄邵陵王綸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Liang's Emperor Yuan Di pressed his elder brother, Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Emperor Yuan Di of Liang turned on his elder brother, Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun.

sentences.zh: 綸北度，與其前西陵郡守羊思達要隨、陸土豪段珍寶、夏侯珍洽，合謀送質于齊，欲來寇掠。

translations.literal: Lun crossed north and with his former prefect of Xiling commandery Yang Sida joined the local magnates of Sui and Lu, Duan Zhenbao and Xiahou Zhenqia, in a plot to send a hostage to Qi and come raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Lun fled north and, with his former Xiling prefect Yang Sida and the local magnates Duan Zhenbao and Xiahou Zhenqia of Sui and Lu, plotted to send a hostage to Northern Qi and launch raids.

sentences.zh: 汝南城主李素，綸故吏也，開門納焉。

translations.literal: Ruyang's city chief Li Su, Lun's former subordinate, opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su, chief of Ruyang and a former follower of Xiao Lun, opened the gates and let him in.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝密報太祖，太祖乃遣忠督衆討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan Di secretly reported to the Grand Progenitor, and the Grand Progenitor thereupon dispatched Zhong to command the host in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan Di secretly informed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, who sent Yang Zhong to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 詰旦陵城，日昃而尅。

translations.literal: At dawn he stormed the city; by the time the sun slanted westward it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the city at dawn and took it before sunset.

sentences.zh: 擒蕭綸，數其罪而殺之；

translations.literal: He captured Xiao Lun, counted his crimes, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xiao Lun, recited his crimes, and executed him;

sentences.zh: 幷獲其安樂侯昉，亦殺之。

translations.literal: and also captured his Prince of Anle Fang and killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: and also captured Prince of Anle Fang and killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 初，忠之擒柳仲禮，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong had captured Liu Zhongli, he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhong had captured Liu Zhongli, he had treated him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 仲禮至京師，乃譖忠於太祖，言其在軍大取金寶珍玩等。

translations.literal: When Zhongli reached the capital, he thereupon slandered Zhong to the Grand Progenitor, saying that in the army he had greatly taken gold, jewels, and precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Zhongli reached the capital he slandered Yang Zhong to Yuwen Tai, claiming he had looted gold, jewels, and precious objects on campaign.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲覆按之，惜其功高，乃出忠。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to investigate thoroughly, but valued his merit as too high and thereupon released Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wanted a full investigation but, unwilling to punish so great a servant, let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 忠忿恚，悔不殺仲禮。

translations.literal: Zhong was resentful and angry, and regretted not having killed Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong was furious and regretted not having killed Liu Zhongli when he had the chance.

sentences.zh: 故至此獲綸等，竝加戮焉。

translations.literal: Thus upon reaching this place, they captured Lun and the others, and all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching this place they captured Xiao Lun and his followers and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 忠間歲再舉，盡定漢東之地。

translations.literal: Zhong within the year mounted two campaigns and fully pacified the lands east of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Yang Zhong launched two campaigns and fully pacified the lands east of the Han.

sentences.zh: 寬以御衆，甚得新附之心。

translations.literal: He was lenient in governing the host and greatly won the hearts of the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He governed his troops with leniency and won the loyalty of the newly submitted peoples.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，賜姓普六如氏，行同州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei's reign, he was granted the surname of the Piliuru clan and acted as governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong of Wei first took the throne, he was granted the surname Piliuru and acted as governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 及于謹伐江陵，忠為前軍，屯江津，遏其走路。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling, Zhong served as vanguard, encamped at the river crossing, and blocked their escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling, Yang Zhong led the vanguard, encamped at the river crossing, and cut off the enemy's escape routes.

sentences.zh: 梁人束刃於象鼻以戰，忠射之，二象反走。

translations.literal: The Liang men bound blades to elephants' trunks to fight; Zhong shot them, and two elephants turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang troops tied blades to their elephants' trunks to fight; Yang Zhong shot at them, and two elephants turned and fled.

sentences.zh: 及江陵平，朝廷立蕭詧為梁

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, the court installed Xiao Cha as Liang
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, the court installed Xiao Cha as Liang

translations.literal: (Wang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wang]

sentences.zh: 〔主〕，令忠鎮穰城以為掎角之勢。

translations.literal: [Lord], and ordered Zhong to garrison Rangcheng to form a pincer position.
translations.idiomatic: lord, and ordered Yang Zhong to garrison Rangcheng in a pincer position.

sentences.zh: 別討沔曲諸蠻，皆克之。

translations.literal: Separately he attacked the various barbarians along the bends of the Mian, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He separately attacked the tribal peoples along the Mian River and subdued them all.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，入為小宗伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Zhong entered the capital as junior chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Yang Zhong entered the capital as junior chief steward.

sentences.zh: 齊人寇東境，忠出鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Qi men raided the eastern frontier, Zhong went out to garrison Puban.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi raided the eastern frontier, Yang Zhong went out to garrison Puban.

sentences.zh: 及司馬消難請降，忠與柱國達奚武援之。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan requested surrender, Zhong together with pillar of state Daxi Wu went to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan offered to surrender, Yang Zhong and pillar of state Daxi Wu went to support him.

sentences.zh: 於是共率騎士五千，人兼馬一疋，從間道馳入齊境五百里。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they led five thousand horsemen, each man with one horse, and by a hidden road galloped five hundred li into Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Together they led five thousand horsemen, each with one mount, and by a hidden route galloped five hundred li into Qi territory.

sentences.zh: 前後遣三使報消難而皆不反命。

translations.literal: Before and after they sent three envoys to report to Xiaonan, yet none returned with reply.
translations.idiomatic: They sent three envoys in succession to notify Sima Xiaonan, but none returned.

sentences.zh: 去〔北〕豫州三十里，武疑有變，欲還。

translations.literal: Thirty li from [Northern] Yuzhou, Wu suspected there was a change and wished to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Northern Yuzhou, Daxi Wu suspected treachery and wanted to turn back.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「有進死，無退生。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "To advance is to face death; to retreat is to find no life.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong said: "Advance and we may die; retreat and we cannot live—

sentences.zh: 」獨以千騎夜趨城下，四面峭絕，徒聞擊柝之聲。

translations.literal: " He alone with a thousand horsemen galloped to the city by night; on all four sides the cliffs were sheer, and they heard only the sound of watchmen's clappers.
translations.idiomatic: " He alone took a thousand horsemen and galloped to the city by night. Cliffs rose sheer on every side; they heard only the watchmen's clappers.

sentences.zh: 武親來，麾數百騎以西。

translations.literal: Wu came in person and waved several hundred horsemen westward.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu came in person and waved several hundred horsemen westward.

sentences.zh: 忠勒餘騎不動，候門開而入，乃馳遣召武。

translations.literal: Zhong restrained the remaining horsemen and did not move; he waited until the gate opened and entered, then galloped to summon Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong held the remaining horsemen still, waited for the gate to open and entered, then galloped off to summon Daxi Wu.

sentences.zh: 時齊鎮城伏敬遠勒甲士二千人據東陴，舉烽嚴警。

translations.literal: At the time Qi's garrison commander Fu Jingyuan mustered two thousand armored soldiers and held the eastern battlement, raising beacon fires in strict alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Qi garrison commander Fu Jingyuan mustered two thousand armored soldiers on the eastern wall and raised beacon fires in full alarm.

sentences.zh: 武憚之，不欲保城，乃多取財帛，以消難及其屬先歸。

translations.literal: Wu feared this and did not wish to hold the city; he therefore took much wealth and silk, and sent Xiaonan and his followers back first.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu feared this and did not want to hold the city; he loaded up wealth and silk and sent Sima Xiaonan and his followers back first.

sentences.zh: 忠以三千騎為殿，到洛南，皆解鞍而臥。

translations.literal: Zhong with three thousand horsemen served as rearguard; when they reached the south of the Luo, all dismounted saddles and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong covered the retreat with three thousand horsemen; reaching the south bank of the Luo, all dismounted and lay down.

sentences.zh: 齊衆來追，至於洛北。

translations.literal: The Qi host came in pursuit as far as the north of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forces pursued them to the north bank of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 忠謂將士曰：「但飽食，今在死地，賊必不敢渡水當吾鋒。

translations.literal: Zhong told the officers and soldiers: "Just eat your fill; we are now in dead ground—the bandits surely will not dare cross the water to meet our edge.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong told his officers and men: "Eat your fill. We stand in dead ground—the enemy will not dare cross the river to meet our attack.

sentences.zh: 」齊兵陽若渡水，忠馳將擊之，齊兵不敢逼，遂徐引而還。

translations.literal: " The Qi army pretended as if to cross the water; Zhong galloped forward to strike them, the Qi army did not dare press close, and so they slowly withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The Qi army feigned a crossing; Yang Zhong galloped forward to strike, the Qi troops did not dare press close, and they slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 武歎曰：「達奚武自是天下健兒，今日服矣！

translations.literal: Wu sighed and said: "Daxi Wu is himself the world's stalwart warrior—today I am convinced!
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu sighed and said: "Daxi Wu is the finest warrior under heaven—and today I am convinced!

sentences.zh: 」進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: " He was advanced in rank to pillar of state and grand general.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Zhong was advanced to pillar of state and grand general.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進封隨國公，邑萬戶，別食竟陵縣一千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng (559), he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Sui with a fief of ten thousand households, separately receiving one thousand households of Jingling county and collecting its rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng (559) he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Sui with ten thousand households, with an additional thousand households in Jingling county whose rents and taxes he collected.

sentences.zh: 尋治御正中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director of the palace steward office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed director of the palace steward office.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，遷大司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding (562), he was transferred to grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding (562) he was transferred to grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時朝議將與突厥伐齊，公卿咸曰：「齊氏地半天下，國富兵強。

translations.literal: At the time court deliberations wished to ally with the Turks to attack Qi; the court ministers all said: "The Qi clan holds half the empire; the state is rich and the army strong.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated allying with the Turks to attack Qi; the ministers all said: "The Qi hold half the empire—their state is rich and their army strong.

sentences.zh: 若從漠北入幷州，極為險阻，且大將斛律明月未易可當。

translations.literal: If one enters Bing Province from the northern desert, it is extremely perilous, and the great general Hulu Mingyue is not easily matched.
translations.idiomatic: An advance from the northern desert into Bing Province would be extremely perilous, and the great general Hulu Mingyue would not be easily matched.

sentences.zh: 今欲探其巢窟，非十萬不可。

translations.literal: To probe their nest now, no fewer than one hundred thousand would do.
translations.idiomatic: To strike at their heartland would require no fewer than one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 」忠獨曰：「師克在和不在衆，萬騎足矣。

translations.literal: " Zhong alone said: "Victory in an army lies in harmony, not in numbers—a ten-thousand-horse force is enough.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Zhong alone said: "An army wins through unity, not numbers—ten thousand horsemen are enough.

sentences.zh: 明月豎子，亦何能為。

translations.literal: Mingyue is a mere stripling—what can he do.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue is a mere stripling—what can he do?

sentences.zh: 」三年，乃以忠為元帥，大將軍楊纂、李穆、王傑、爾朱敏及開府元壽、田弘、慕容延等十餘人皆隸焉。

translations.literal: " In the third year, Zhong was made commander-in-chief; grand generals Yang Zuan, Li Mu, Wang Jie, Erzhu Min, and opening-office holders Yuan Shou, Tian Hong, Murong Yan, and more than ten others all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year Yang Zhong was made commander-in-chief; grand generals Yang Zuan, Li Mu, Wang Jie, Erzhu Min, and opening-office holders Yuan Shou, Tian Hong, Murong Yan, and more than ten others all served under him.

sentences.zh: 又令達奚武帥步騎三萬，自南道而進，期會晉陽。

translations.literal: Daxi Wu was also ordered to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by the southern road to advance, with a rendezvous at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu was also ordered to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by the southern route, to rendezvous at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 忠乃留敏據什賁，遊兵河上。

translations.literal: Zhong then left Min to hold Shifen and sent roaming troops along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong left Erzhu Min to hold Shifen and sent roaming detachments along the river.

sentences.zh: 忠出武川，過故宅，祭先人，饗將士，席捲二十餘鎮。

translations.literal: Zhong went out from Wuchuan, passed his old residence, sacrificed to his ancestors, feasted the officers and soldiers, and swept through more than twenty garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong marched out from Wuchuan, visited his old home, sacrificed to his ancestors, feasted his officers and men, and swept through more than twenty garrisons.

sentences.zh: 齊人守陘嶺之隘，忠縱奇兵奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Qi men defended the narrow pass at Xingling; Zhong unleashed surprise troops in a fierce assault and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi defended the narrow pass at Xingling; Yang Zhong sent surprise troops in a fierce assault and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 又留楊纂屯靈丘為後拒。

translations.literal: He also left Yang Zuan to encamp at Lingqiu as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also left Yang Zuan encamped at Lingqiu as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 突厥木汗可汗控

translations.literal: The Turkic Muhan Khan together with
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Muhan Khan together with

translations.idiomatic: [variant: Ye]

translations.literal: [Di]tou Khan and Bu
translations.idiomatic: Ditou Khan and Bu

translations.idiomatic: [variant: Sui]

translations.literal: [Li] Khan and others, with one hundred thousand horsemen, came to join.
translations.idiomatic: Buli Khan and others came to join with one hundred thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 四年正月朔，攻晉陽。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fourth year, they attacked Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fourth year they attacked Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是時大雪數旬，風寒慘烈，齊人乃悉其精銳，鼓噪而出。

translations.literal: At this time heavy snow fell for several tens of days; wind and cold were bitter; the Qi men then mustered all their picked troops, beating drums and shouting as they came out.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell for weeks; wind and cold were bitter. The Qi mustered all their picked troops, beating drums and shouting as they sallied forth.

sentences.zh: 突厥震駭，引上西山不肯戰。

translations.literal: The Turks were shaken with terror, withdrew up Western Mountain, and refused to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were terrified, withdrew up Western Mountain, and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 衆皆失色。

translations.literal: The host all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army turned pale.

sentences.zh: 忠令其衆曰：「事勢在天，無以衆寡為意。

translations.literal: Zhong ordered his host: "The situation lies with Heaven; do not take account of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong told his troops: "Fortune lies with Heaven—do not count numbers.

sentences.zh: 」乃率七百人步戰，死者十四五。

translations.literal: " He then led seven hundred men in infantry combat; one in four or five died.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led seven hundred men in foot combat; four or five in ten fell.

sentences.zh: 以武后期不至，乃班師。

translations.literal: Because Wu was late and did not arrive, he thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Daxi Wu was late and never arrived, he withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 齊人亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: The Qi men also did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces also did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 突厥於是縱兵大掠，自晉陽至

translations.literal: The Turks then let their troops plunder widely, from Jinyang to
translations.idiomatic: The Turks then let their troops plunder freely from Jinyang to

translations.idiomatic: [variant: Luan]

sentences.zh: 〔平〕城七百餘里，人畜無孑遺，俘斬甚衆。

translations.literal: [Ping]cheng, over seven hundred li—people and livestock left none surviving; captives slain were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Pingcheng, more than seven hundred li—people and livestock were wiped out; captives and slain were very many.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使迎勞忠於夏州。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sent envoys to welcome and reward Zhong at Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent envoys to welcome and reward Yang Zhong at Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 及至京師，厚加宴賜。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he was lavishly feasted and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he was lavishly feasted and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 高祖將以忠為太傅，晉公護以其不附己，難之，乃拜總管涇

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was about to appoint Zhong as grand tutor; Duke of Jin Hu, because he did not attach himself to Hu, objected, and so appointed him commander of all military affairs in the six provinces of Jing
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was about to appoint Yang Zhong grand tutor, but Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, finding that he would not attach himself to Hu, objected; instead he was appointed commander of all military affairs in the six provinces of Jing

translations.literal: (You)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: You]

sentences.zh: 〔豳〕靈雲鹽顯六州諸軍事、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: [Bin], Ling, Yun, Yan, and Xian, and governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, Ling, Yun, Yan, and Xian, and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大軍又東伐，晉公護出洛陽，令忠出沃野以應接突厥。

translations.literal: That year the great army again campaigned east; Duke of Jin Hu went out from Luoyang and ordered Zhong to go out from Woye to link with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: That year the main army campaigned east again; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu marched from Luoyang and ordered Yang Zhong out from Woye to coordinate with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 時軍糧旣少，諸將憂之，而計無所出。

translations.literal: At the time army grain was already scarce; the generals were anxious, yet no plan could be found.
translations.idiomatic: Army grain was already scarce; the generals were worried but could find no solution.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「當權以濟事耳。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "One must use expedients to accomplish the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong said: "We must use an expedient to get through this.

sentences.zh: 」乃招誘稽胡諸首領，咸令在坐。

translations.literal: " He thereupon summoned and enticed the various Ji Hu chieftains, all ordering them to be seated.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned the Ji Hu chieftains and had them all seated.

sentences.zh: 使王傑盛軍容，鳴鼓而至。

translations.literal: He sent Wang Jie to display full military array and arrive beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Jie to arrive with full military display, beating drums.

sentences.zh: 忠陽怪而問之。

translations.literal: Zhong feigned surprise and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong feigned surprise and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 傑曰：「大冢宰已平洛陽，天子聞銀、夏之間生胡擾動，故使傑就公討之。

translations.literal: Jie said: "The Grand Preceptor has already pacified Luoyang; the Son of Heaven heard that raw Hu between Yin and Xia were stirring in disorder, and therefore sent Jie to join the Duke in punishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie said: "The grand preceptor has already pacified Luoyang. The Son of Heaven heard that unruly Hu between Yin and Xia were stirring up trouble, and sent me to join you in punishing them.

sentences.zh: 」又令突厥使者馳至而告曰：「可汗更入幷州，留兵馬十餘萬在長城下，故遣問公，若有稽胡不服，欲來共公破之。

translations.literal: " He also had a Turkic envoy gallop up and report: "The khan has again entered Bing Province and left more than one hundred thousand troops and horses below the Great Wall; therefore he sends to ask the Duke—if there are Ji Hu who will not submit, he wishes to come and join the Duke in breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: " He also had a Turkic envoy gallop up and announce: "The khan has again entered Bing Province and left more than one hundred thousand troops below the Great Wall. He sends to ask you—if any Ji Hu will not submit, he wishes to come and join you in crushing them.

sentences.zh: 」坐者皆懼，忠慰喻而遣之。

translations.literal: " Those seated were all afraid; Zhong comforted and instructed them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: " Those seated were all terrified; Yang Zhong reassured them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 於是諸胡相率歸命，饋輸填積。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Hu one after another submitted; tribute and transport piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Hu submitted one after another, and supplies piled up.

sentences.zh: 屬晉公護先退，忠亦罷兵還鎮。

translations.literal: Just then Duke of Jin Hu withdrew first; Zhong also ceased troops and returned to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu had already withdrawn; Yang Zhong also ceased operations and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 又以政績可稱，詔賜錢三十萬、布五百疋、穀二千斛。

translations.literal: Again because his administrative achievements were commendable, an edict granted three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Because his administrative record was commendable, an edict granted him three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 弟整，建德中，開府、陳留郡公，從高祖平齊，歿於幷州。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zheng, during Jian'e, was opening-office, Duke of Chenliu commandery; he followed the High Ancestor in pacifying Qi and died at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yang Zheng, during the Jian'e era, held opening-office rank and the title Duke of Chenliu; he followed Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi and died at Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 以整死王事，詔其子智積襲其官爵。

translations.literal: Because Zheng died in the king's service, an edict ordered his son Zhiji to inherit his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Zheng died in imperial service, an edict ordered his son Zhiji to inherit his office and title.

translations.idiomatic: Yang Zheng's younger brother

translations.idiomatic: [variant: Hui]

translations.idiomatic: Hui, at the end of the Daxiang era, was chief steward and Duke of Jingling county.

translations.literal: (Hui)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Hui]

sentences.zh: 〔慧〕弟嵩，以忠勳，賜爵興城郡公，早卒。

translations.literal: [Hui]'s younger brother Song, on account of Zhong's merit, was granted the marquisate of Xingcheng commandery and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Song, on Yang Zhong's merit, was granted the marquisate of Xingcheng commandery and died young.

sentences.zh: 嵩弟達，亦以忠勳，爵周郡公。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Da, also on account of Zhong's merit, held the rank of Duke of Zhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Da, also on Yang Zhong's merit, held the title Duke of Zhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 王雄字胡布頭，太原人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong, courtesy name Hubutou, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong, courtesy name Hubutou, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父侖以雄

translations.literal: His father Lun, on account of Xiong's
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun, on account of Xiong's

translations.literal: outstanding merit, was posthumously awarded pillar of state and grand general, junior tutor, and Duke of Ankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: heroic merit, was posthumously awarded pillar of state and grand general, junior tutor, and Duke of Ankang commandery.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖接喪亂之際，乘戰爭之餘，發迹平涼，撫征關右。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Grand Progenitor received the age amid mourning and disorder, rode the remainder of war, rose from Pingliang, and pacified and campaigned in the lands west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai rose amid chaos and war, started from Pingliang, and pacified the lands west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 于時外虞孔熾，內難方殷，羽檄交馳，戎軒屢駕。

translations.literal: At that time external invaders blazed fiercely and internal troubles were still pressing; urgent dispatches flew back and forth and the war chariot was repeatedly driven forth.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign enemies pressed hard and internal troubles still raged; urgent dispatches flew back and forth and the war chariot was repeatedly driven forth.

sentences.zh: 終能蕩清逋孽，克固鴻基。

translations.literal: In the end he was able to sweep clear lingering evils and firmly consolidate the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he swept away lingering enemies and firmly consolidated the dynasty's foundation.

sentences.zh: 雖稟筭於廟謨，實責成於將帥。

translations.literal: Although plans were received in the temple counsels, achievement was truly charged to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Though strategy was laid in the council chamber, the achievement truly rested with the generals.

sentences.zh: 達奚武等竝兼資勇略，

translations.literal: Daxi Wu and the others all combined courage and stratagem,
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu and the others all combined courage and stratagem,

translations.literal: (Gan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Gan]

sentences.zh: 〔咸〕會風雲。

translations.literal: [Xian] met the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: and met the opportune moment.

sentences.zh: 或效績中權，或立功方面，均分休慼，同濟艱難。

translations.literal: Some achieved merit at the central command, some established merit on the frontiers; they shared joy and sorrow equally and together crossed hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Some served at the center of power, others won glory on the frontiers; they shared joy and sorrow and together endured hardship.

sentences.zh: 可謂國之爪牙，朝之禦侮者也。

translations.literal: They can be called the state's claws and fangs, the court's defense against insult.
translations.idiomatic: They were truly the state's claws and fangs, the court's bulwark against insult.

sentences.zh: 而武協規太祖，得儁小

translations.literal: Yet Wu coordinated plans with the Grand Progenitor and secured the narrow
translations.idiomatic: Yet Daxi Wu coordinated plans with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and secured the narrow

translations.literal: (Jian)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Jian]

sentences.zh: 〔關〕，周瑜赤壁之謀，賈詡烏巢之策，何能以尚。

translations.literal: [Guan] pass—the stratagems of Zhou Yu at Red Cliffs and Jia Xu's plan at Wucao Nest—how could these compare.
translations.idiomatic: Guan pass—the stratagems of Zhou Yu at Red Cliffs and Jia Xu's plan at Wucao Nest—how could these compare?

sentences.zh: 一言興邦，斯近之矣。

translations.literal: One word can raise a state—this comes close to it.
translations.idiomatic: One word can raise a state—this comes close to that.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
